content: Slaves and Masters EPHESIANS 6:5-9 âIN A CONSCIOUS SHIFT FROM PAULâS DIRECTION FOR WIVES IN CHAPTER 5 to submit, in chapter 6 of Ephesians he tells children and slaves to obey. This may be seen as a recognition that in the ancient world of the Bible children and slaves had even less status than women.â â Snodgrass/TAR WHILE I BELIEVE THIS IS AN ACCURATE OBSERVATION, I THINK it is even more important to keep in mind that âAll relations in the social household codes are redefined by oneâs relation to Christ.â â Snodgrass/TAR IN THIS WEEKâS BLOG WE WILL STUDY THE RELATIONSHIP OF âSLAVES AND MASTERS.â On first hearing you might be inclined to think the passage doesnât apply to us. If that is your mindset here at the beginning, I think youâll be surprised. ONE COMMENTATOR TITLES THIS PASSAGE, âSPIRIT-FILLED LABOR RELATIONSHIPSâ (MacArthur). Iâd like us to expand the literal words of âSlaves and Mastersâ to include the dimension of worker and boss, by extension, to all employee-employer relationships. I think youâll soon agree the passage permits this rephrasingâ¦ NAS Ephesians 6:5-9 Slaves, be obedient to those who are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as to Christ; 6 not by way of eyeservice, as men-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart. 7 With good will render service, as to the Lord, and not to men, 8 knowing that whatever good thing each one does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether slave or free. 9 And, masters, do the same things to them, and give up threatening, knowing that both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with Him. âIN THIS PASSAGE PAUL GIVES HIS FINAL ILLUSTRATION OF THE principle of Spirit-produced mutual submission.â â MacArthur âTHIS SECTION MAKES SPECIFIC TO SLAVES â AND TO MASTERS â WHAT was asked of everyone in chapter 5, vv. 10, 17, and 21, which is pleasing the Lord, doing His will, and mutual submission.â Snodgrass NAS Ephesians 5:10 trying to learn what is pleasing to the Lord. NAS Ephesians 5:17 So then do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is. NAS Ephesians 5:21 and be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. WE MUST REMEMBER THE POINT MADE PREVIOUSLY: All relationships for the believer must be defined by their relationship with their Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. WE MUST ALSO REALIZE THAT âTo apply mutual submission to slaves and slave owners was a startling redefinition of slavery for Paulâs readers. In 1 Corinthians 7:21â23 Paul even told slaves that slavery should not matter, that they were Christâs freed people, that both free and slaves were slaves of Christ, and therefore that they should not be slaves of humans!â â Snodgrass NAS 1 Corinthians 7:21-23 Were you called while a slave? Do not worry about it; but if you are able also to become free, rather do that. 22 For he who was called in the Lord while a slave, is the Lordâs freedman; likewise he who was called while free, is Christâs slave. 23 You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men. IF WE WERE FIRST CENTURY RECIPIENTS OF PAULâS LETTERS, we would most likely be shocked by Paulâs words. The apostle pulled no punches. âTHE EASE WITH WHICH PAUL MADE THESE POINTS WAS BASED ON his conviction that slaves, their owners, and he, himself, were all slaves of Christ. Paul referred to himself frequently as a slave of Christ.â â Snodgrass. Consider Paulâs introduction to his letter to the Romans for exampleâ¦ NET Romans 1:1 From Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God. NET Philippians 1:1 From Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with the overseers and deacons. NET Titus 1:1 From Paul, a slave of God and apostle of Jesus Christ, to further the faith of Godâs chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that is in keeping with godliness, I HAVE ALWAYS THOUGHT THAT PAULâS GREETINGS ARE especially beautifulâ¦ Think of it: here was the most important, authoritative, powerful Christian in the world writing letters to churches and how does he introduce himself? Î Î±á¿¦Î»Î¿Ï , Î´Î¿á¿¦Î»Î¿Ï á¼¸Î·ÏÎ¿á¿¦ ÏÏÎ¹ÏÏÎ¿á¿¦ ( Pau-los, dou-los Yeah-sou Chris-tos ): Paul, slave of Jesus Christâ¦ ALL âTHIS REALLY SHOULD NOT BE SURPRISING INSOFAR AS CHRIST HIMSELF took the form of a slave.â â Snodgrassâ¦ NAS Mark 10:45 âFor even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve , and to give His life a ransom for many.â I WANT TO SPEND ANOTHER MOMENT ON THIS SUBJECT. Not only is the slave important to our passage but the slave image is central to our relationship to Christ. WHEN I DIE, I have asked my dear wife and family to engrave on my tombstone âBond slave of Jesus Christââ¦ THE BACKGROUND FOR THIS SLAVE THEOLOGY COMES FROM THE O.T. For example, these words from Leviticus 25:55â¦ NAS Leviticus 25:55 âFor the sons of Israel are My servants; they are My servants whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God. THE HEBREW WORD FOR âSERVANTâ IS ×¢Ö¶×Ö¶× ( eh-ved ). It is used some 800 times in the O.T., 340 more times in the Greek LXX (Septuagint). Thatâs a lot. While the word is often translated âservant,â it is more properly translated âslave.â I believe when the Bible is carefully studied throughout both the Old and New Testaments, it is shown that âslaveâ is a superior translation of the Greek word Î´Î¿á¿¦Î»Î¿Ï ( dou-los ) in Ephesians and more in keeping with the believerâs relationship to God. An even more accurate translation, I believe, would be âbond slave.â A BONDSLAVE IS A PERSON WHOIS OBLIGATED TO A MASTER WITHOUT WAGES, one who gives himself up to anotherâs will, devoted to another at the disregard of oneâs own interest (Strongâs Enhanced). That aptly describes the believer, especially the Christian. SO IMPORTANT IS THE GREEK WORD Î´Î¿á¿¦Î»Î¿Ï ( dou-los ), a few more words about it are, I think, are warranted. The very word slave indicates subjection and usually bondage. The old KJV Bible translates the word âservant,â so traditionally most Christians probably think of their relationship to Christ in servant terms. Thatâs OK; itâs just not as accurate as it could and should be in my humble opinion. I think youâll agree there are differences between servant and slave . A servant is usually paid, for one thing. And a servant can usually quit his job. Not so with slaves. The Greek word Î´Î¿á¿¦Î»Î¿Ï ( dou-los ) does not bear the connotation of a free individual serving another. The BDAG Greek lexicon notes that ââservantâ for âslaveâ is largely confined to Biblical translation and early American times when the word âslaveâ was usually avoided. But in normal usage at the present time the two words are carefully distinguished.â (from NET Notes). IT IS CERTAINLY TRUE THAT WE SERVE THE LORD, BUT when the relevant biblical words are carefully studied in context, primarily we do so not as servants but as slaves. âIN BIBLICAL TIMES SLAVERY WAS COMMON AND MUCH ABUSED. In both Greek and Roman cultures, most slaves had no legal rights and were treated as commercial commodities. Roman citizens came to look on work as beneath their dignity, and the entire empire gradually came to function largely by slave power. Slaves were bought, sold, traded, used, and discarded as heartlessly as if they were animals or tools. Considerate masters who were deeply grieved over the death of some of their slaves were exceptional.â â MacArthur âBECAUSE SUCH A LARGE PROPORTION OF THE ROMAN EMPIRE CONSISTED of slaves, it is likely that the proportion in the church was large also. This social phenomenon contained the seeds of many conflicts for the church; perhaps the greatest of these occurred when both master and slave were Christians. The proclamation that in Christ there is neither âslave nor free manâ (Col 3:11; Gal 3:28) must have caused many a disapproving glance by a by a slave toward his master.â â Kent NAS Galatians 3:28 There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is

title: Children and Parents
excerpt: Children and Parents EPHESIANS 6:1-4 WE HAVE COMPLETED THE FIRST FIVE CHAPTERS of Paulâs letter to the Ephesians, so today we will be looking at the opening verses of chapter six, the last chapterâ¦ NAS Ephesians 6:1-4â¦
content: Children and Parents EPHESIANS 6:1-4 WE HAVE COMPLETED THE FIRST FIVE CHAPTERS of Paulâs letter to the Ephesians, so today we will be looking at the opening verses of chapter six, the last chapterâ¦ NAS Ephesians 6:1-4 Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. 2 Honor your father and mother (which is the first commandment with a promise), 3 that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the earth. 4 And, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger; but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord. I HAVE TITLED THIS BLOG âCHILDREN AND PARENTS.â You may remember that the previous passage in Ephesians, 5:22-33, was entitled, âWives and Husbands.â Therefore, the subject matter of our passage this week is fitting. I WANT TO EMPHASIZE THAT THESE WORDS FROM VV. 1-4 DO NOT COME FROM modern, secular psychology, worldly anthropology, or the latest liberal study on the education of children, but from Scripture. This is the Word of God on the relationship of âChildren and Parentsââ¦ âPAUL TAUGHT THE BELIEVERS AT EPHESUS (modern Turkey) to give careful attention to how they lived. They were not to live unwisely but rather wisely because the times were full of evil. They must live carefully. The believers must know Godâs will and live in that will. Godâs will was that Christians allow the Holy Spirit to control their lives. One evidence of the Holy Spiritâs control was that believers would submit âto one another in the fear of Christ.ââ â Garner NAS Ephesians 5:21 and be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. SUBMISSION IS A BIG TOPIC IN THIS SECTION OF EPHESIANS. AS WE LEARNED IN OUR PREVIOUS MESSAGE ON âWIVES AND HUSBANDS,â Paul wanted a general submissiveness to prevail among the families in the Ephesian church. The apostle first addressed the relationship between husbands and wives. Paul then continued to explain how letting the Holy Spirit control oneâs life impacts relationships between children and parents as well as between slaves and masters.â â Garner NEXT WEEKâS BLOG WILL BE TITLED JUST THAT: âSlaves and Masters.â âBIBLICAL SUBMISSION IS ALWAYS TO BE A TWO-WAY STREET. The Word of God never says to one party only, âSubmit.â Submission is always to be mutual among Godâs people.â â Steadman/TAR THE COMMON SENSE OF THIS PASSAGE IS REMARKABLE! It is remarkable mainly because common sense sadly is too often not a prevailing factor in our society today, as most I think would agree. THE GREEK WORD FOR âOBEYâ ( á½ÏÎ±ÎºÎ¿á½»Ï [ hoo-pa-koo-o ]) means to follow instruction, to follow, and to be subject to . âOBEDIENCE IS A CRUCIALLY IMPORTANT MATTER IN SCRIPTURE, as you should know, especially though not exclusively in the O.T. All through the Word of God you find exhortations to parents to teach their children to be obedient, and exhortations for children to be responsive to that teaching and obey their parents. In Scripture, a child must learn the most important lesson of all: to be an obedient, respectful child.â â Steadman/TAR CONSIDER THOSE WORDS IN CONTRAST TO OUR SOCIETY TODAY. Further comment is, I think, hardly necessary. Just compare children in movies and on TV today. They are invariably smart alecks who always have the upper hand on their parents. Respect for parents, much less obedience to parents, is almost never seen. MOST COMMENTATORS BELIEVE THAT PAULâS WORDS SPRING FROM EXODUS 20:12 (in the LXX; Deut 5:16 is also a possibility)â¦ NAS Exodus 20:12 âHonor your father and your mother, that your days may be prolonged in the land which the LORD your God gives you. BUT I THINK IT IS WRONG TO FOCUS ON JUST ONE O.T. VERSE for the source of Paulâs exhortations to the Ephesians. I think it is more accurate to keep in mind that Paulâs words reflect a general truth found often and stressed often in the O.T. For example, consider these few selected passages form the O.T. that speak directly and indirectly to the prominent point of obedience of children to their parentsâ¦ NAS Leviticus 19:3 âEvery one of you shall reverence his mother and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths; I am the LORD your God. NAS Deuteronomy 21:18-21 âIf any man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother, and when they chastise him, he will not even listen to them, 19 then his father and mother shall seize him, and bring him out to the elders of his city at the gateway of his home town. 20 âAnd they shall say to the elders of his city, âThis son of ours is stubborn and rebellious, he will not obey us, he is a glutton and a drunkard.â 21 âThen all the men of his city shall stone him to death; so you shall remove the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear of it and fear. NAS Exodus 21:15 âAnd he who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. NAS Exodus 21:17 âAnd he who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. NAS Proverbs 1:8 Hear, my son, your fatherâs instruction, And do not forsake your motherâs teaching; NAS Proverbs 5:1 My son, give attention to my wisdom, Incline your ear to my understanding; rebuke. NAS Proverbs 13:24 He who spares his rod hates his son, But he who loves him disciplines him diligently. THERE IS NO QUESTION THAT PAUL IS MERELY REFLECTING GODâS WILL for children and parents as repeatedly spelled out in the O.T. BACK TO EPHESIANS 6:1â¦ âNOTICE CAREFULLY THAT THIS IS NOT A SIMPLE EXHORTATION FOR children to obey their parents. It goes a step further. The text reads, âChildren, obey your parents in the Lord.â Just as wives are to submit to their husbands as unto the Lord, and just as husbands are to love their wives after the example of the Lord, so it is with children: They are to obey their parents for Jesusâ sake.â â Steadman/TAR âTHE PHRASE âIN THE LORDâ DOES NOT MEAN THAT children are to obey parents only if their parents are believers. As Colossians 3:20 clearly denotes, a childâs obedience to his parents is pleasing in the Lordâs sight.â â Hoehner (B.K.C.) NAS Colossians 3:20 Children, be obedient to your parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing to the Lord. ONE OBSERVATION I WOULD MAKE: Although I believe it may be convincingly shown that Paul â and Scripture in general â has in mind in such passages younger children, it is nevertheless true that there are no conditions placed upon the command. Commands in the Bible are not conditional, not to be applied in certain situations and dismissed in others. Godâs commands are all- encompassing, unconditional. I believe the Bible strongly implies that these commands to children to obey and honor their parents extend throughout the lives of both. NOTE FINALLY IN V. 1 THE WORDS, âFOR THIS IS RIGHTââ¦ âThe reason for this is that it is âright.â It is a proper course of action to follow in society.â â Hoehner (B.K.C.). The obedience of children to their parents strengthens society, just as the disobedience of children to their parents inevitably weakens society. BUT I THINK MAYBE THE SIMPLEST, MOST DIRECT INTERPRETATION OF these words is that Paul is saying that obedience produces positive results. âIf children obey their parents, everything will turn out right. If they refuse to do so, everything will go wrong, because disobedience to parents violates one of the fundamental laws of living.â â Steadmanâ¦ CONSIDER AGAIN EXODUS 20:12â¦ NAS Exodus 20:12 âHonor your father and your mother, that your days may be prolonged in the land which the LORD your God gives you. AND THAT IS ALMOST EXACTLY WHAT PAUL SAYS IN EPHESIANS 6:2-3 as he quotes from this familiar O.T. passageâ¦ promise), that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the earth. âGLAD, WILLING, SINCERE OBEDIENCE, WITH AN ATTITUDE OF HONOR AND respect, creates the conditions that tend to produce a long, healthy, happy life. Obedient children tend to live constructively and productively, and they are less likely to fall prey to self-destructive temptations and snares, such as alcoholism, drug abuse, juvenile crime, l

excerpt: Wives and Husbands EPHESIANS 5:22-33 WE HAVE COME TO END OF CHAPTER 5 IN OUR VERSE-BY-VERSE STUDY OF the great book of Ephesians: Godâs Word for this weekâs blog is vv. 22-33 of Ephesians 5â¦ NAS Ephesians 5:22-33 Wives,â¦
content: Wives and Husbands EPHESIANS 5:22-33 WE HAVE COME TO END OF CHAPTER 5 IN OUR VERSE-BY-VERSE STUDY OF the great book of Ephesians: Godâs Word for this weekâs blog is vv. 22-33 of Ephesians 5â¦ NAS Ephesians 5:22-33 Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord. 23 For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body. 24 But as the church is subject to Christ, so also the wives ought to be to their husbands in everything. 25 Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her; 26 that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, 27 that He might present to Himself the church in all her glory, having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing; but that she should be holy and blameless. 28 So husbands ought also to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself; 29 for no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the church, 30 because we are members of His body. 31 For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh. 32 This mystery is great; but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the church. 33 Nevertheless let each individual among you also love his own wife even as himself; and let the wife see to it that she respect her husband. WHAT AN INCREDIBLE PASSAGE THAT IS: Godâs Word on marriage. As I studied these words this week I could not get away from that fact. This is Godâs Word and Godâs will â not manâs word and manâs will â on how marriage should be. âLIFE IS MADE MEANINGFUL BY RELATIONSHIPS, the most meaningful of which is that between a man and a woman. In 1 Peter 3:7, the apostle Peter calls the husband-wife relationship âthe grace of life.ââ â MacArthur NAS 1 Peter 3:7 You husbands likewise, live with your wives in an understanding way, as with a weaker vessel, since she is a woman; and grant her honor as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered. I WONDER JUST HOW MANY MARRIED COUPLES THINK OF THEIR MARRIAGE relationship as âthe grace of life.â A marriage that continually gets better, richer, and more satisfying is rare today, as most of us well know. âFROM MANY VOICES TODAY COMES THE CLAIM THAT the very institution of marriage has failed to meet peopleâs needs. But the fact is that it is not a matter of marriage having failed, since marriage, as we can easily see today in our âsophisticatedâ culture, has been increasingly avoided. Now, as you well know, it is acceptable to live together in place of marriage. Today, in place of exerting consistent effort and determination to fulfill the commitment it takes to make oneâs marriage work, the solution is to bail out.â â MacArthur/TAR TODAY WE SEE SIGNS ADVERTISING FAST DIVORCES, âQUICKY DIVORCES.â It is common to hear in our society today people say, âWe tried, but it just didnât work out. âCommitmentâ has become a word that is considered old-fashioned and impractical today. â IN HIS BOOK Becoming Partners: Marriage and its Alternatives, Dr. Carl Rogers writes from the view of a humanistic unbeliever, âTo me it seems we are living in an important and uncertain age, and the institution of marriage is most assuredly in an uncertain state. If 50-75 percent of Ford or General Motors cars completely fell apart within the early part of their lifetimes as automobiles, drastic steps would be taken. We have no such well-organized way of dealing with our social institutions, so people are groping, more or less blindly, to find alternatives to marriage, which by all accounts is certainly less than 50 percent successful. Living together without marriage, extensive childcare centers, serial monogamy (one divorce after another), the womenâs liberation movement to establish the woman as person in her own right, divorce laws that do away with the concept of guilt â these are all gropings toward some new form of man-woman relations for the future.ââ â MacArthur WE HAVE 12 VERSES TO COVER TODAY. These 12 verses constitute the context of the âWives and Husbandsâ relationship and should be taken as a whole. We will take these 12 verses 3 verses at a time, with v. 33 being singled out as the summary verse. First, vv. 22-24. These verses deal with âThe Role and Priorities of the Wifeâ (MacArthurâs title for this section of the passage)â¦ NAS Ephesians 5:22-24 Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord. 23 For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body. 24 But as the church is subject to Christ, so also the wives ought to be to their husbands in everything. IâD LIKE TO REMIND YOU HOW PAUL FINISHED THE PREVIOUS PASSAGE, our blog from last week on âFilled by the Spirit.â In v. 21, Paul wroteâ¦ NAS Ephesians 5:21 and be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. I TOLD YOU LAST WEEK THAT V. 21 NOT ONLY ENDS THE PASSAGE on filling but sets the tone for the following passages, going through 6:9. Whereas the mindset today, orchestrated by the womenâs liberation movement and the media, is selfish individualism, mutual submission is the message of the Bible. I MUST TELL YOU THAT THE WORD âSUBMITâ DOES NOT APPEAR IN V. 22 in the Greek text (the Critical Text, the family of ancient texts from which we get all our modern English translations but two) most valued today by Greek scholars (it does, however, appear in the Majority Text from which we get the King James and the New King James texts). There is not a main verb in v. 22, something that usually occurs in the both groupings of Greek texts. However, the word âsubmitâ is most definitely found in v. 21 and may be said to be the controlling thought of what follows. Note that the word is present â it is not italicized â in v. 24. So, even though the word is not found in v. 22 it is legitimate to insert the italicized word. The bottom line is there is no question that whichever ancient or modern text one prioritizes, this is Paulâs thought. NOTE ALSO THE LITTLE WORD âFORâ IN V. 23. This little word, which could also be translated âbecause,â gives us the reason for the wivesâ submission. âHeadship implies authority. A home without direction is chaotic just as a nation without a ruler or an army without a commander. According to the Scriptures, the husbandâs task is being the wifeâs head and thus the familyâs head just as Christ is the head and has authority over the church.â â Garnerâ¦ LISTEN AGAIN TO EPHESIANS 1:22â¦ NAS Ephesians 1:22 And He put all things in subjection under His feet, and gave Him as head over all things to the church, AND EPHESIANS 4:15â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:15 but speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him, who is the head, even Christ, CHRIST IS THE HEAD OF CHURCH; LIKEWISE THE HUSBAND IS TO BE HEAD of the family. WHILE THAT IS TRUE, IT IS ALSO IMPORTANT TO REMEMBER a crucial difference between Christâs headship and that of the husbandâ¦ âCHRIST IS LORD OVER ALL THINGS; THE HUSBAND IS NOT LORD of anything. âChrist is Lord over all things; the husband is not lord of anything. The point of the headship analogy is the responsibility husbands have to give themselves to their wives as Christ gave Himself for the church. Husbands are to be givers, not takers.â â Snodgrass AT THE RISK OF OVER-STAYING MY WELCOME, I invite you to read thoughtfully verses 22-24 againâ¦ KEEPING IN MIND THIS IS THE WORD OF ALMIGHTY AND ALL-LOVING GODâ¦ NAS Ephesians 5:22-24 Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord. 23 For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body. 24 But as the church is subject to Christ, so also the wives ought to be to their husbands in everything. title: Be Strong and Courageous
excerpt: Be Strong and Courageous JOSHUA 1:1-9 HAPPY NEW YEAR! AS YOU WELL KNOW, THIS WEEK MOVING WE ARE MOVING INTO 2018. Thanks be to God for bringing us through another year. No matter what trials we may be experiencing, weâ¦
content: Be Strong and Courageous JOSHUA 1:1-9 HAPPY NEW YEAR! AS YOU WELL KNOW, THIS WEEK MOVING WE ARE MOVING INTO 2018. Thanks be to God for bringing us through another year. No matter what trials we may be experiencing, we all have reason to be grateful this morning and to be positive about the year ahead. All Christians, regardless of circumstances, should be positive people. We are the only people who have valid reason for optimism. IT IS COMMON FOR BELIEVERS AND UNBELIEVERS ALIKE TO SEEK guidance from an allegedly reliable source, or at least think seriously about positively reordering their lives on the auspicious occasion the New Year naturally affords. ALONG THESE AMELIORATING LINES, I SUGGEST THE TITLE of this biblical blog for inspirational words to consider. THE TITLE COMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT BOOK OF JOSHUA, the first nine verses of the first chapterâ¦ NAS Joshua 1:1-9 Now it came about after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD that the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Mosesâ servant, saying, and all this people, to the land which I am giving to them, to the sons of Israel. 3 âEvery place on which the sole of your foot treads, I have given it to you, just as I spoke to Moses. 4 âFrom the wilderness and this Lebanon, even as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun, will be your territory. 5 âNo man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I have been with Moses, I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you. 6 âBe strong and courageous, for you shall give this people possession of the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. 7 âOnly be strong and very courageous; be careful to do according to all the law which Moses My servant commanded you; do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may have success wherever you go. 8 âThis book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do according to all that is written in it; for then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have success. 9 âHave I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous! Do not tremble or be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.â AND FROM DEUTERONOMY, THIS RELEVANT COMMENTâ¦ NAS Deuteronomy 34:8 So the sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end. THE PREAMBLE: Verses 1-9 are termed âThe Preambleâ by many commentators. âPreambleâ means 1. A preliminary statement, especially the introduction to a formal document that serves to explain its purpose. 2. An introductory occurrence or fact; a preliminary. âAfter the death of Moses the Lord summoned Joshua, the servant of Moses, whom He had appointed as the leader of Israel into Canaan, to go with all the people across the Jordan, and take the land which had been promised to the fathers on oath, assuring him at the same time of His powerful aid, on condition that he observed the law of Moses faithfully. This summons and promise of God form the preamble to the whole book, which is linked on to the conclusion of the Pentateuch by the introductory words, âAnd it came to pass after the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord,â though it is not so closely connected as to warrant the conclusion that the two works have been written by the same authorâ (Keil & Delitzsch)â¦ CANAAN, OF COURSE, IS THE LAND WE NOW CALL âISRAELâ? âSERVANT OF THE LORD.â Moses is called âthe servant of the Lord.â This is a special title that is often applied to Moses. The Hebrew word for âservantâ is not particularly revealing (Ö´××× [ eh-ved ]) in and of itself; it means slave or trusted servant. But when the word is traced carefully throughout the Pentateuch (the first 5 books of the Bible), it may be seen that the servant of the Lord was âthe loftiest title attainable in a community which acknowledged the sovereignty of God alone. It implied faithful obedience to God in all things with special reference to leadership of the people of Israel in matters pertaining to the covenant.â â Southern Baptist Commentary JOSHUA IS TO SUCCEED TO THE HIGH TASK OF SERVANT . Previously, Joshuaâs role had been that of Mosesâ minister. We might think of Joshua as a special assistant to Moses, a kind of military lieutenantâ¦ NKJ Exodus 24:13 So Moses arose with his assistant Joshua, and Moses went up to the mountain of God. NAS Exodus 33:11 Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, just as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses returned to the camp, his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent. NOW, AT THE CALL OF GOD, JOSHUA WAS TO ASPIRE TO the high task of servant of the Lord himself. Even the special title of âthe servant of the Lordâ would be eventually granted to himâ¦ NAS Joshua 24:29 And it came about after these things that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD , died, being one hundred and ten years old. YES, âTHE SERVANT OF THE LORDâ IS A SPECIAL TERM. All of us should seek these special words. We are all children of God, having been born again by faith in Christ, but we should want also to be servants of the Lord. Special wordsâ¦ THIS NEW YEARS WEEK WE WILL LOOK AT MORE SPECIAL WORDS: âBe Strong and Courageous.â OF ALL THE MEMORABLE CLAUSES AND PHRASES OF THE BIBLE, this clause we will study this week is certainly one of the most memorable: âBe Strong and Courageous.â So central to the book of Joshua is this clause that it is found four times in the first chapter (vs. 6, 7, 9, 18)â¦ NAS Joshua 1:6 âBe strong and courageous, for you shall give this people possession of the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. 6 IS THE RESULT OF V. 5â¦ V. 6 is because of v. 5â¦ NAS Joshua 1:5 âNo man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I have been with Moses, I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you. GOD PROMISED NOT ONLY THE LAND; HE PROMISED HIS PRESENCEâ¦ Because God would be with Joshua and the Israelites, it was possible for them to be strong and courageousâ¦ ONLY BECAUSE WE TOO AS BELIEVERS ARE PROMISED Godâs presence can we be truly strong and courageous. IN THE BOOK OF JOSHUA WE GET A GOOD PICTURE OF HOW GOD works. title: Consider Christmas
excerpt: Consider Christmas LET US CONSIDER CHRISTMAS TOGETHER. âCONSIDERâ means to think carefully about, especially in order to make a decision; it means to contemplate, to ponder, to bear in mind. And in a biblical context, Iâ¦
content: Consider Christmas LET US CONSIDER CHRISTMAS TOGETHER. âCONSIDERâ means to think carefully about, especially in order to make a decision; it means to contemplate, to ponder, to bear in mind. And in a biblical context, I believe, it is accurate to add this serious and productive mental activity is supposed to lead to decision, and then action. FIRST, I WOULD LIKE FOR US TO NOTICE THE PARTICULAR CARE THE BIBLE TAKES IN SPEAKING ABOUT THE LORD JESUS CHRIST. Scripture does not just simply say that Christ was born. I ask you to notice the precision (not one but three descriptive clauses) in which the Scripture employs to refer to His birth in a unique way â PLEASE CONSIDERâ¦ NAS John 1:1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. âIN BEGINNINGâ â There is no article in the Greek text. Although in Greek grammar that fact does not mean the object of the preposition âin,â âbeginning,â is, therefore, indefinite, But this fact does not necessarily limit Christâs beginning to the time of the creation of the world. It is possible that in the Greek by this initial prepositional phrase John is carrying our thoughts beyond the beginning of creation in time to eternity, which it is correct to say had no beginning. Time exists within eternity. Suffice it to say that whichever beginning is meant, the Word was present. The Bible never attempts to prove Godâs existence; it is just assumed. Isnât that beautiful? There is such strong proof of deity alluded to in this unique unspoken assumption. âWASâ â Three times in the first verse of his gospel, John significantly uses the imperfect tense of the Greek word ÎµÎ¹Î¼Î¹ ( eye â me ), which means in the present tense âto be.â We will see in a moment that John, also significanty, uses quite a different verb for the beginning of the Incarnation of God. The Greek imperfect here conveys no idea of origin for God or the Logos (the Word), but simply continuous existence in the past. In other words, God Himself had no beginning: He simply and profoundly was . We find the same idea inâ¦ ESV John 8:58 Jesus said to them, âTruly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am.â John 8:58, according to the imperfect tense of the verb (Greek has four past tenses, whereas English has one), could be translated âBefore Abraham was, I AM . Before Abraham was, I was existing timelessly . âTHE WORDâ â âTHE LOGOSâ â Î»Î¿Î³Î¿Ï is a common Greek word widely employed by ordinary people and scholars alike. John was speaking to both groups, informing the former and refuting and correcting the latter (e.g., Philo) The Greek word Î»Î¿Î³Î¿Ï ( log â os ) has always been a point of special interest to me. WHAT DOES âTHE WORDâ IN THIS SPECIAL CONTEXT MEAN? Exactly how are we to envision Christ as the Word? A WORD SERVES TWO DISTINCT PURPOSES : 1) It expresses a concept; it is a sound or sounds that gives expression to a perception â if it is not verbalized (or, by extension, written) it remains a concept. THINK OF A WORD AS A THOUGHT WITH CLOTHES ON; A WORD IS A THOUGHT CLOTHED: CHRIST IS GOD âFLESHEDâ 2) A word reveals the thought . JESUS CHRIST SHOWED US GOD: COLOSSIANS 1:15 â âHe is the image of the invisible God.â JOHN 14:9 â âHe who has seen Me has seen the Father.â JOHN 10:30 â âI and My Father are one.â âAND THE WORD WAS WITH GOD.â â In the Greek the construction presents another example of the language of precison and exaltation which uniformly surrounds the Lord Jesus. When the Greek grammar and context are studied, it may be seen that the seemingly innocuous prepositional phrase, âwith God,â suggests intimacy. We could think of the Word and God being face to face with each other . The phrase denotes a special relationship of eternal fellowship in the Trinity. Who could claim this privileged familiarity with God other than God? The next clause gives us the answerâ¦ âAND THE WORD WAS GOD.â â In the Greek the predicate is before the subject in order to emphasize Christâs full deity . He was of the same quality as God. What is being stressed here is that the Word is in possession of the full nature of God. WHY DID I FRAME THIS CHRISTMAS BLOG FROM JOHN 1:1? BECAUSE I WANT US TO KEEP IN THE FOREFRONT OF OUR THOUGHTS AS WE CONSIDER CHRISTMAS, THE FACT THAT JESUS WAS MUCH MORE THAN THE HISTORICAL BABE OF BETHLEHEM; HE WAS AND IS GOD ALMIGHTY. Unlike the other three gospels which begin with a historical reference, John begins with a theological prologue. It is as if John was saying âI want you to consider the teachings and deeds of the Lord Jesus Christ, but before you can do this accurately you must understand His Person: the things He said and the things He did are those of the God-Man.â MY HUMBLE TRANSLATION OF JOHN 1:1: âTHE WORD IS ETERNAL; THE WORD IS IN RELATIONSHIP TO GOD (THE FATHER); AND THE WORD IS GOD.â NAS John 1:14 And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. WHAT I WOULD LIKE YOU TO SEE HERE IS THE CAREFULNESS THE BIBLE USES TO DESCRIBE THE INCARNATION (âINCARNATIONâ MEANS âENFLESHMENTâ): THE VERSE DOES NOT SAY: âAND THE WORD WAS FLESH.â VERB : âThe Greek verb has a very special meaning here. It is not âbecameâ in the sense of ceasing to be what it was before. THE WORD BECOMES FLESH BUT REMAINS THE WORD . EXAMPLE : (Remember Pastor Mattâs sermon on Genesis 19 a couple of weeks ago? It sets the stage: ESV Genesis 19:26 But Lotâs wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.) When the wife of Lot became a pillar of salt, she ceased to be the wife of Lot. Thatâs one way to use the word. That is not the way the word âbecameâ is used in John 1:14. When Lot became the father of Moab and Ammon, he remained Lot. Thatâs the way the word is used here. THE WORD BECAME FLESH BUT REMAINED THE WORD .â â Hendriksen HOW COULD THIS BE: TWO NATURES? Jesus is the only being that possessed both a divine and human nature, He is the unique God-Man. He had to be 100% human to be our representative and He had to be 100% God to be the perfect, sinless sacrifice for our sins. ESV 1 Timothy 3:16 Great indeed, we confess, is the mystery of godliness: He was manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory. I TITLED THIS BLOG âCONSIDER CHRISTMASâ WE HAVE CONSIDERED: 1) WHO â THAT CHRIST IS GOD â JOHN 1:1 2) WHAT â THAT HE BECAME A MAN â JOHN 1:14 NOW LET US CONSIDERâ¦ 3) WHY â WHY GOD BECAME A MAN â WHY THERE IS A CHRISTMAS: NAS John 3:16-17 âFOR GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD, THAT HE GAVE HIS ONLY BEGOTTEN SON, THAT WHOEVER BELIEVES IN HIM SHOULD NOT PERSISH, BUT HAVE ETERNAL LIFE. 17 FOR GOD DID NOT SEND HIS SON INTO THE WORLD TO JUDGE THE WORLD, BUT THAT THE WORLD SHOULD BE SAVED THROUGH HIM.â THIS, I SUGGEST, IS A SUMMARY OF THE GOSPEL BECAUSE IT IMPLICITLY TELLS US THE PURPOSE OF CHRISTâS COMING, THE PRIZE HE SECURED FOR US THROUGH HIS UNSPEAKABLE SACRIFICE, AND THE WAY WE RECEIVE THAT INCOMPARABLE GIFT OF LOVE â BY FAITH! âCONSIDER CHRISTMASâ AND THEN ACT UPON YOUR CONSIDERATION BY BELIEVING THE GOSPEL AND PLACING YOUR TRUST IN CHRIST. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY WE TRULY EXPERIENCE CHRISTMAS! LOVE âWhat kind of God could shape the earth and stars? Yet watch oâer the sparrow as it flies? What kind of Father could forgive the failing heart And dry the tears that sinners cry? What kind of Lord would build for us a place With seas of glass and mansions high? What kind of Friend would save us from the grave By giving His own Son to die? If eyes could know one glimpse of heavenâ¦ He must be beauty and splendor He must have strong hands that guide with gentle touch He must be hopeâ¦ and He must be joyâ¦ But more than these, He must be LOVE. FOR GOD SO LOVEDâ¦ HE GAVEâ¦ NAS Matthew 1:21 âAnd she will bear a Son; and you shall call His name Jesus, for it is He who will save His people from their sins.â JESUS WAS âBORN TO DIEâ WITHOUT SIN THERE WOULD BE NO CHRIST

title: Filled by the Spirit
excerpt: filled by the Spirit EPHESIANS 5:18-21 SPIRIT FILING IS ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL TO LIVING THE CHRISTIAN LIFE. âEssentialâ means absolutely necessary, indispensable . Essential suggests that which is in the very essence orâ¦
content: filled by the Spirit EPHESIANS 5:18-21 SPIRIT FILING IS ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL TO LIVING THE CHRISTIAN LIFE. âEssentialâ means absolutely necessary, indispensable . Essential suggests that which is in the very essence or constitution of a thing, WITHOUT EXAGGERATION, THIS PASSAGE IS CENTRAL TO OUR FAITH AND our understanding of our lives in Christ. It is impossible to overstate the importance of Spirit-filling. The main passage in the New Testament defining Spirit-filling for New Testament believers is Ephesians 5:18-21â¦ NAS Ephesians 5:18-21 And do not get drunk with wine, for that is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit, 19 speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord; 20 always giving thanks for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father; 21 and be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. IF YOU ARE NOT SPIRIT FILLED , you cannot claim to be obediently or effectively living the Christian life. Every Christian should be able to say, âYes, I am Spirit filled!â If you are not now âFilled by the Spirit,â I would ask you why not? Spirit filling is a choice. God commands to be âFilled by the Spiritâ; therefore, it is our choice whether to obey or not. You decide whether or not you are âFilled by the Spirit/â âNO CHRISTIAN CAN FULFILL GODâS WILL FOR HIS OR HER LIFE APART FROM being filled with (better âbyâ â TAR) His Spirit. If we do not obey this command, we cannot obey any other â simply because we cannot do any of Godâs will apart from Godâs Spirit.â â MacArthur IS IT âWITHâ THE SPIRIT OR âBYâ THE SPIRIT? In my Greek classes I have taught this passage for many years. Greek scholars for years have argued how the prepositional phrase should be interpreted. Forgive the technical detail, but I would like you to get a sense of the scope of the argument, and in order to do so, some technical detail is necessary. The following paragraph is exemplary: âMany have taken á¼Î½ ÏÎ½Îµá½»Î¼Î±ÏÎ¹ ( en pneu-ma-ti â the key prepositional phrase that may be correctly translated either by, with, in the Spirit â TAR) as indicating content, i.e., one is to be filled with the Spirit. But there are no other examples in biblical Greek in which á¼Î½ ( en ) + the dative after ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ; I fill) indicates content. Further, the parallel with Î¿á¼´Î½á¿³ ( oi-no ; wine) as well as the common grammatical category of means suggest that the idea intended is that believers are to be filled by means of the [Holy] Spirit. If so there seems to be an unnamed agent. The meaning of this text can only be fully appreciated in light of the ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ) language in Ephesians. â NET Notes I ADMIT THIS IS HEAVY STUFF! Nevertheless, I hope you will read on. Remember, please, God chose the Greek language, not English or Spanish, to reveal Himself in the New Testament. THERE ARE THREE KEY CONSIDERATIONS THAT MAY HELP US UNDERSTAND what Paul is saying in this passage of Ephesians 5:18. (1) In Eph 3:19 the âhingeâ prayer introducing the last half of the letter makes a request that the believers âbe filled with all the fullness of Godââ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:19 and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled up to all the fullness of God. THE EXPLICIT CONTENT OF THE GREEK VERB ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ) IS THUS Godâs fullness, which is probably a reference to His moral attributes. In other words, it is God who fills us and it is with Himself by which He fills us. NOW LETâS LOOK AT 4:10 , the second key consideration (2)â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:10 He who descended is Himself also He who ascended far above all the heavens, that He might fill all things.) NOTE THAT IN 4:10 CHRIST IS SAID TO BE THE AGENT OF FILLING (with v. 11 adding the specifics of his giving spiritual gifts). Paul then brings his argument to a crescendo in 5:18: âBelievers are to be filled by Christ by means of the Spirit with the content of the fullness of Godââ¦ (3) AND THE THIRD KEY CONSIDERATIONâ¦ âTHE GREEK WORD TRANSLATED âBE FILLEDâ ( ÏÎ»Î·ÏÎ¿á¿¦ÏÎ¸Îµ [ play-rous-thay ] from the verb ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï [ play-ra-o ]) is a command in a form ( present passive imperative ) in the original language that means âkeep on being filled by the Spirit.ââ â Garner/TARâ¦ ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ) âIS USED IN THE N.T. OF SOMETHING THAT IS FILLED WITH content, for example, âto fillâ containers or, in the passive as in John 12:3â¦â â Hoehnerâ¦ NAS John 12:3 Mary therefore took a pound of very costly perfume of pure nard, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped His feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume. IT IS THE IMAGE OF SOMETHING BEING PERVADED BY SOMETHING ELSE. When we are filled by the Spirit we are pervaded by the Spirit. Pervade means to be present throughout. When we are filled the Spirit is present throughout our being. âMETAPHORICALLY, IN THE PASSIVE ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ) CAN MEAN to be filled with something, such as unrighteousness.â â Hoehner NAS Romans 1:29 being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; they are gossips, ÏÎ»Î·Ïá½¹Ï ( play-ra-o ) THUS âMAY BE SEEN TO CONNOTE THE IDEA THAT a person is completely controlled and stamped by the powers which fill him.â âHoehner from Delling THE ESSENCE IS THAT WE ARE TO LIVE UNDER THE CONTROL OF THE SPIRIT, not under the wineâs control. I would humbly suggest that it is a graphic and immediately apprehended analogy â agree? INTOXICATION ONLY LEADS TO RECKLESS ACTIONS. âDissipationâ (á¼ÏÏÏá½·Î± [ a-so- tee-a ]) may be seen to mean (among other connotations) recklessness. Paul, in v. 17, commanded the Ephesians â and by extension us â to avoid such foolish conductâ¦ NAS Ephesians 5:17 So then do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is. âAS IS HIS PRACTICE. PAUL NOT ONLY INSTRUCTS BELIEVERS CONCERNING the way in which they are not to live, but also how they are to live. He had told the Ephesians not to be unwise but wise, not to become foolish but to understand what the will of the Lord is, not to be drunk with wine in which there is dissipation but â the positive exhortation â be filled by the Spirit.ââ Hoehnerâ¦ THE BIBLE CONDEMNS DRUNKENNESS. Here are but two examplesâ¦ NAS Proverbs 23:19-21 Listen, my son, and be wise, And direct your heart in the way. 20 Do not be with heavy drinkers of wine, Or with gluttonous eaters of meat; 21 For the heavy drinker and the glutton will come to poverty, And drowsiness will clothe a man with rags. NAS Isaiah 5:11 Woe to those who rise early in the morning that they may pursue strong drink; Who stay up late in the evening that wine may inflame them! â THE HOLY SPIRIT IS THE MEANS BY WHICH BELIEVERS ARE FILLED WITH Christ and His will.â â Hoehnerâ¦ Note again v.17â¦ NAS Ephesians 5:17 So then do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is. âTHIS IS FITTING BECAUSE THE PARALLEL PASSAGE OF THE PRESENT VERSE, Colossians 3:16, also written by Paul, statesâ¦â â Hoehnerâ¦ NAS Colossians 3:16 Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you, with all wisdomâ¦ BEING FILLED BY THE SPIRIT IS SUCH A CRUCIAL TRUTH TO GRASP. As I said at the beginning, it is indispensable. If we are ever to experience success and satisfaction in our Christian lives we must be continually âFilled by the Spirit.â THE IMPERATIVE MOOD â THE FACT THAT ITâS A COMMAND â places the responsibility for being filled squarely upon us as believers. The passive voice shows tells us that we cannot fill ourselves; we must be submissive to God and allow Him to fill us, to control us. BEING âFILLED BY THE SPIRITâ ENABLES GOD TO PRODUCE IN US THE FRUIT of the Spiritâ¦ NAS Galatians 5:22-23 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, 23 gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. CHRISTLIKENESS . When the Holy Spirit controls the life of the believer His fruit will be produced in that life. Being filled by the Spirit wil

title: Walk in Wisdom
excerpt: Walk in Wisdom EPHESIANS 5:15-17 OUR PASSAGE THIS THIS FROM THE BOOK OF EPHESIANS AGAIN DEALS WITH how we should walk, more specifically what the âworthy walkâ should look like. You may remember Paulâs foundationalâ¦
content: Walk in Wisdom EPHESIANS 5:15-17 OUR PASSAGE THIS THIS FROM THE BOOK OF EPHESIANS AGAIN DEALS WITH how we should walk, more specifically what the âworthy walkâ should look like. You may remember Paulâs foundational practical admonition in chapter 4, verse 1â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:1 I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, entreat you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling with which you have been called, PAUL GOES ON TO SAY IN CHAPTER 4 THAT BELIEVERS ARE ALSO TO âWALK in Unityâ (4:1-16). Then in chapter 5, he commands Christians to âWalk in Loveâ (5:1-2), âWalk in Purityâ (4:17-32; 5:3-7), and Walk in Lightâ (5:8-14). Now, in our message this week from chapter 5, verses 15-17, Paul exhorts his readers â and us to day â to âWalk in Wisdomââ¦ NAS Ephesians 5:15-17 Therefore be careful how you walk, not as unwise men, but as wise, 16 making the most of your time, because the days are evil. 17 So then do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is. â VERSE 15 SERVES AS THE BASIS FOR THE MANY EXHORTATIONS FOUND in the rest of chapter 5 and the first 9 verses of chapter 6.â â Hoehner/TARâ¦ PAUL SAID A SIMILAR THING IN HIS LETTER TO THE COLOSSSIANS. First from the NKJâ¦ NKJ Colossians 4:5 Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time. COLOSSIANS 4:5 FROM THE NASâ¦ NAS Colossians 4:5 Conduct yourselves with wisdom toward outsiders, making the most of the opportunity. AND FINALLY FROM THE NIV TRANSLATIONâ¦ NIV Colossians 4:5 Be wise in the way you act toward outsiders; make the most of every opportunity. A PARAPHRASE OF THIS VERSE FROM COLOSSIANS MIGHT BE , âBe tactful and wise in all your relations with unbelievers; buy up every possible opportunity to influence them for the kingdom of God.â â Harris (A âparaphraseâ is a round-about way of saying something.) THESE THREE DIFFERENT TRANSLATIONS GIVE US AN IDEA OF WHAT THE WORD âwalkâ means in the N.T. Our âwalkâ is how we conduct ourselves, how we act and speak. Our âwalkâ is the visible outgrowth of what we believe. If we have truly been saved and if we have any idea of Godâs grace in saving us, we should want to âWalk Worthy.â THE GREEK WORD FOR âWALKâ IS THE VERB ÏÎµÏÎ¹ÏÎ±Ïá½³Ï ( pe-ri-pa-tay-o Ã ). It is found 969times in the N.T. Thatâs a lot. Literally, it means to walk up and down, to walk about . The Gospels and Acts use the word mainly in this literal way. Consider these three examplesâ¦ NAS Matthew 4:18 And walking by the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen. NAS Matthew 14:25 And in the fourth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea. NKJ John 5:11 He answered them, âHe who made me well said to me, âTake up your bed (âpalletâ â NAS) and walk.â â THE NAS TRANSLATES ÏÎµÏÎ¹ÏÎ±Ïá½³Ï ( pe-ri-pa-tay-o Ã ) âPROWLâ IN 1 PETER 5:8â¦ NAS 1 Peter 5:8 Be of sober spirit , be on the alert. Your adversary, the devil, prowls about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. THE NKJ TRANSLATION READSâ¦ NKJ 1 Peter 5:8 Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. BUT PAUL AND JOHN IN THEIR LETTERS TO THE CHURCH USE THE WORD âWALKâ metaphorically. Walk is a common idiom for oneâs lifestyle, behavior, or manner of conduct. Here are a few examplesâ¦ NKJ Romans 8:4 that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. NKJ 2 Corinthians 5:7 For we walk by faith, not by sight. YOUâRE PROBABLY FAMILIAR WITH THIS PASSAGE FROM 1 JOHNâ¦ NKJ 1 John 1:6-7 If we say that we have fellowship with Him, and walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. âWHAT BELIEVERS ARE GIVES CREDIBILITY TO WHAT THEY SAY. Believers are to exhibit a carefully planned, consistent, righteous Christian life. It is only if believers live wisely will the watching world see the power of God working in them.â â MacArthur THAT IS SO VERY IMPORTANT FOR US TO UNDERSTAND. Our profession of faith in Christ, while it means everything to us, means nothing to the outside world. Unbelievers are interested very little if at all in what we say, but they cannot ignore what we do. CONSIDER FOR A MOMENT THE âWALKâ OF CHRISTIAN LEADERS. Consider how much a good walk influences people. I know in my life I thank the Lord daily for faithful men God has placed in my life, especially men like David Jeremiah, George Hare, and Gary Coombs. The faithful, wise walk of these men â without a word being exchanged â inspire me and hold me accountable to walk in the same manner. Such faithful walks are noticed by the unbelieving world, though unbelievers rarely if ever acknowledge the fact. THE OBVIOUS QUESTION THEN IS âWHAT IS BIBLICAL WISDOMâ? The Greek word is ÏÎ¿Ïá½·Î± ( sa-fee-a ). BDAG, the leading Greek lexicon in the world today, defines ÏÎ¿Ïá½·Î± ( sa-fee-a ) as 1. the capacity to understand and function accordingly, wisdom that God imparts to those who are close to God. It is used 51 times in the N.T. in a variety of ways (218 times in both Testaments). For example, did you know that unbelievers can have wisdom? The only problem is, worldly wisdom is not acceptable by Godâ¦ NAS 1 Corinthians 3:19 For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. For it is written, â He is the one who catches the wise in their craftinessâ; BUT MOSTLY IN THE BIBLE WISDOM REFERS TO GOD AND BELIEVERS. Most often wisdom is portrayed as desirable; we are exhorted to acquire wisdomâ¦ NKJ Proverbs 4:7 Wisdom is the principal thing; Therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding. JESUS IN HIS HUMANITY WAS FILLED WITH WISDOMâ¦ NKJ Luke 2:40 And the Child grew and became strong in spirit, filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was upon Him. AND, AGAIN KEEP IN MIND WE ARE TALKING OF HIM IN HIS HUMANITY, the Bible says Jesus âgrew in wisdomââ¦ NAS Luke 2:52 And Jesus kept increasing (imperfect tense â TAR) in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men. A BRIEF, TO-THE-POINT DEFINITION OF âWISDOMâ IS FEARING or reverencing God and applying Godâs Word to practical situations of life. Wisdom in the Bible has much more to do with practicality than it does intelligenceâ¦ IN STUDYING âWISDOMâ ONE FINDS IT IS NOT THE EASIEST WORD TO DEFINE . âThough wisdom and the wise men who perpetuate it have been around almost as long, if not as long as have people, the study of wisdom in the ancient Near East is a relatively new endeavor. This has been due, in part, to a lack of clear definition of the term âwisdom,â as well as the difficult nature of the poetic language within which most of the wisdom material is found.â â Holman Illustrated Bible Dictionary â¦ WHERE DOES WISDOM COME FROM? As you might imagine, it comes from Godâ¦ NAS Proverbs 2:6 For the LORD gives wisdom; From His mouth come knowledge and understanding. âAS BELIEVERS IMMERSE THEMSELVES IN THE LIFE OF CHRIST, it is wisdom that will enable us to determine just how, in given situations, our new way of thinking, our new set of values, should be put into effect.â â Moo WISDOM IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE OBEDIENT, EFFECTIVE BELIEVER. NAS Ephesians 5:15 Therefore be careful how you walk, not as unwise men, but as wise, ââBE CAREFULâ COMES FROM A COMMON GREEK WORD ( Î²Î»á½³ÏÏ [ blep-po ]) that refers to seeing. Here, it refers to spiritual perception. excerpt: Walk in Light EPHESIANS 5:8-14 I TITLED ANOTHER BLOG âWALK IN LIGHTâ LAST YEAR AT CHRISTMASâ¦ As Iâm sure you would agree, a large number of passages from Scripture have to do with the believerâs intimate associationâ¦
content: Walk in Light EPHESIANS 5:8-14 I TITLED ANOTHER BLOG âWALK IN LIGHTâ LAST YEAR AT CHRISTMASâ¦ As Iâm sure you would agree, a large number of passages from Scripture have to do with the believerâs intimate association with light, understandably so, for God is lightâ¦ NAS Psalm 89:15 How blessed are the people who know the joyful sound! O LORD, they walk in the light of Thy countenance. ESV John 9:5 As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.â AS WE HAVE BEEN LEARNING THESE PAST WEEKS, Paulâs favorite analogy to communicate his exhortations to believers is referring to the Christian life as a walk. In chapters 4 and 5, Paul has already encouraged the Ephesians to âWalk Worthyâ (4:1), âWalk in Unityâ (4:1-16), âWalk in Loveâ (5:1-2), and âWalk in Purityâ (4:17-32; 5:3-7). In our passage for this morning, vv. 8-14 of chapter 5 of Ephesians, Paul exhorts his readers â and us today â to âWalk in Light.â âBELIEVERS ARE CALLED BY PAUL, âCHILDREN OF LIGHTâ (5:8), and they are commanded to demonstrate this fact each day by steadfastly refusing to participate in the sinful actions and attitudes of unbelievers.â â Garner/TAR NAS Ephesians 5:8-14 for you were formerly darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light 9 (for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness and righteousness and truth), 10 trying to learn what is pleasing to the Lord. 11 And do not participate in the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but instead even expose them; 12 for it is disgraceful even to speak of the things which are done by them in secret. 13 But all things become visible when they are exposed by the light, for everything that becomes visible is light. 14 For this reason it says, âAwake, sleeper, And arise from the dead, And Christ will shine on you.â âTHE CHRISTIAN LIFE IS ALWAYS A CALL TO BE WHO GOD SAYS WE ARE.â â Hoehnerâ¦ As I like to say, âWe are not who we think we are; we are who God says we are.â ITâS ANOTHER BIBLICAL CONTRAST. The entire Bible may be said to be a book of contrasts: right and wrong, good and evil, righteous and unrighteous, believers and unbelievers, love and hate, and light and darkness. We were once darkness, but now we are light. THE KJV VERSION OF V. 8â¦ NKJ Ephesians 5:8 For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light IF YOU ARE A BELIEVER, THIS IS YOUR LIFE HISTORY CONDENSED: âYou were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord.â âPAUL IS REMINDING BELIEVERS OF THE GREAT CHANGE THAT HAD OCCURRED when they became Christians. Notice that he does not merely say that they had been âin darkness,â but rather that they âwere darkness.â In their unconverted state they had been so permeated by the realm of evil that they themselves personified that realm. But now as a result of regeneration, of salvation through Christ, they were not only âin the light,â but through their vital union with Christ, who is the light of the world, they themselves are here characterized as âlight.â They share Christâs life and nature, and they exhibit His character.â â Kent KJV John 8:12 Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world : he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO INTELLIGENTLY SPEAK ABOUT LIGHT FROM THE BIBLE without drawing upon the writings of the apostle John. The Greek word for light , Ïá¿¶Ï ( phos ), is used some 70 times in the N.T.; in Johnâs gospel, epistles, and the book of Revelation, are found 31 of them (in Paulâs writings there are 12). Listen to a few more instances from Johnâs writingsâ¦ NAS 1 John 1:5 And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you, that God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all. NAS John 12:46 âI have come as light into the world, that everyone who believes in Me may not remain in darkness. NAS 1 John 1:7 but if we walk in the light as He Himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin. LIKE LIGHT IN THE DARKNESS, OUR LIVES IN CHRIST are to reflect the mind and will of God. WALKING IN LIGHT IS ANOTHER WAY OF SAYING WALKING IN OBEDIENCEâ¦ âThe children of light do the will of God.â â Bruce âWALK IN LIGHTâ MEANS DO WHAT GOD SAYS IN HIS WORD. When we are obedient to Godâs commands in Scripture and surrendered to the power and leadership of the Holy Spirit, then and only then may we say that we are truly walking in light. NAS Ephesians 5:9 (for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness and righteousness and truth), NOTE THAT THE CLAUSE IS ENCASED IN PARENTHESES; it is explaining v. 8.. Verse 9 is telling us what it means to walk as a child of light. Walking in light is marked by or verified by âall goodness and righteousness and truth.â FRUIT IS THE PRODUCT OF AN ACTION. The action is light (genitive of production â Wallace). âIt is the light that produces the fruit. Paul is listing the fruit â goodness, righteousness, and truth â so that believers can measure their lives to see if their actions or works are the result of the light.â â Hoehner IF WE CANNOT LOOK AT OUR LIVES AND SEE GOODNESS, RIGHTEOUSNESS, AND truth, we must ask ourselves, are we really children of light. WHEN YOU CONSIDER THIS VERSE CAREFULLY, IT IS DIFFICULT TO SEE ANY difference in âthe fruit of the lightâ and âthe Fruit of the Spiritââ¦ NAS Galatians 5:22 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, THE FRUIT OF THE LIGHT AND THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT ARE IDENTICAL. They both come from God and both are produced by the believer. FRUIT IS WHAT IS PRODUCED IN THE LIFE OF THE BELIEVER WHEN the believer is submissive to Godâs power residing within. NAS Ephesians 5:10 trying to learn what is pleasing to the Lord. THIS IS SUCH AN AMAZING VERSE, I BELIEVE. I could easily have written a blog just on this single verse, which is subordinate to the main verb âwalkâ in v. 8. âTRYING TO LEARNâ IS A PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. Participles are words that usually describe something, like adjectives. Most of the time, as here in v. 10, they describe or modify verbs. âWalkâ is the main verb of this passage.. âTrying to learnâ is describing âwalkâ; it is showing us âthe manner of the walk of children of light.â â Hoehner LIGHT IN THE BIBLE STANDS FOR GODâS BLESSINGS, PRESENCE, AND revelation (Isaiah 2:9) that is incarnate in Jesus (Isaiah 58:8; 59:90; 60:1-2, 19-20; John 8:12). IN THE BIBLE, THERE IS A TESTING TO BRING ABOUT FAILURE, AND there is a testing unto approval. Satan tests us in hopes we may fail; God tests us to make us stronger so that we may succeed. I think it more precisely conveys the sense of the passage. It is a fact of Scripture that God commonly tests us so that we will grow stronger in some way, sooner or later. God tests us to determine if we are genuine â not so that He might know, of course; He already knows; but that we ourselves might know. THERE IS GREAT WISDOM TO BE REALIZED IN THAT TRUTH â AMEN? excerpt: Thanksgiving 2017 SELECTED PSALMS NAS Psalm 107:1 Oh give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; For His lovingkindness is everlasting. THANKSGIVING 2017â¦ A SPECIAL TIME FOR THE GIVING OF THANKSâ¦ There is only one Personâ¦
content: Thanksgiving 2017 SELECTED PSALMS NAS Psalm 107:1 Oh give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; For His lovingkindness is everlasting. THANKSGIVING 2017â¦ A SPECIAL TIME FOR THE GIVING OF THANKSâ¦ There is only one Person to whom we may truly give thanks, and that is God. To whom do unbelievers thank? A true understanding of Thanksgiving will lead the thinking person to God. God is the source of all good things and ultimately it is to Him and to Him only that we give thanksâ¦ NAS James 1:17 Every good thing bestowed and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation, or shifting shadow. CHRISTIANS LIVING IN AMERICA SHOULD BE ESPECIALLY THANKFUL. Along those lines, I thought you might enjoy hearing Abraham Lincolnâs Thanksgiving Day Proclamation of 1863: ââ¦ No human counsel hath devised, nor hath any mortal hand worked out these great things (Godâs providential care of America). They are the gracious gifts of the most high God, who, while dealing with us in anger for our sins, hath nevertheless remembered mercy.â (MERCY â withholding from us what punishment or condemnation we deserve) CHRISTIAN THANKSGIVING : âThanksgiving â It is gratitude for all the benefits of divine Providence, especially for the general and personal gifts of redemption.â â Ungerâs Bible Dictionary A CHRISTIAN SHOULD NEVER BE AT A LOSS to find things for which to be thankful. The Christian should lives in an âAttitude of Gratitude.â That is the message of the New Testament that is echoed directly and indirectly throughout its pages. Just one exampleâ¦ KJV 1 Thessalonians 5:18 In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. EVERYTHING WE DO SHOULD BE DONE IN A SPIRIT OF THANKSGIVING , recognizing our blessings in Christ. We should always have an âattitude of gratitudeâ â amen? NET Colossians 2:6-7 Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him and firm in your faith just as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness. IF WE ARE NOT LIVING LIKE THAT, WHY NOT? Colossians 2:6-7 and 1 Thessalonians 5:18 are commands. That means thanksgiving is a choice for us: we choose to be obedient to God and be thankful, or we do not. Thanksgiving, like love and forgiveness is not an emotion; it is a choice. These commands from Scripture have nothing to do with our circumstances. The Bible nowhere releases us from our Christian responsibility to be obedient if things happen not to be going our way. JUST THE FACT WE ARE ALIVE and have been granted another day of life should make us thankful continuously throughout the day. THANKSGIVING IS A MINDSET. The mind is the battlefield. We have to train our minds to recognize the positive and not allow ourselves to focus on the negative. NAS Philippians 4:8 Finally, brethren, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good repute, if there is any excellence and if anything worthy of praise, let your mind dwell on these things. THANKSGIVING IS A CHOICE AND THANKSGIVING IS A MINDSET. IT HAS BEEN MY OBSERVATION THAT, SADLY, MANY CHRISTIANS ARE NOT THANKFUL. Many are often times whiners and complainers. Too many Christians only seem to want to talk about the negative. God wants us to be joyous lights in this dark world, thanking Him continuously for the blessings He mercifully and graciously gives us. I know you know this. In great part this blog is a reminder to us, not necessarily a lesson for usâ¦ ESV 2 Peter 1:12 Therefore I intend always to remind you of these qualities, though you know them and are established in the truth that you have. PSALM 69:30 SHOULD BE AN ACCURATE REFLECTION OF ALL OF USâ¦ NAS Psalm 69:30 I will praise the name of God with song, And shall magnify Him with thanksgiving. BRIEFLY, SOME FACTS ABOUT THE MAIN O.T. WORD FOR âTHANKSGIVINGâ¦ ( ya-dah ), basically means âconfession,â either of sin or of Godâs character and works. The term was employed uniquely in reference to the sacrificial system of Israel. One could bring a âthank-offeringâ (or âpraise-offeringâ) in which he would make declarations of praise to God and/or confession of sin to God as he offered his sacrificeâ¦ KJV Leviticus 7:11-12 And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he shall offer unto the LORD. If he offer it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mingled with oil, of fine flour, fried. I WONDER HOW MANY CHRISTIANS THINK OF THEIR THANKSGIVING AS AN OFFERING? SUCH AN OFFERING AND CONFESSION GLORIFIED GOD. It showed His righteousness in contrast to the personâs sin (Psalm 50:23), and was a means by which one ordered his way aright. KJV Psalm 50:23 Whoso offereth praise toe-dah â thanksgiving) glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God. O.T. THANKSGIVING WAS JOYFUL! When the sacrifice was accompanied with praise (confession) of God, it was especially a time of joyâ¦ KJV Psalm 95:1-2 O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms. KJG Jeremiah 33:11 The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say,, Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD. GOD WAS MAGNIFIED BY SUCH PRAISE OF THANKSGIVING; AGAIN PSALM 69:30â¦ KJV Psalm 69:30 I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving. PSALM 100 IS A TYPICAL PSALM OF PRAISE for this type of joyous occasionâ¦ KJV Psalm 100:1 <A Psalm of praise.> Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands. Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing. Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture. Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations. ISNâT THAT A MAGNIFICENT PSALM? O.T. thanksgiving was joyful. OUR FOCUS IN THIS PARTICULAR BLOG IS OLD TESTAMENT, BUT one major thanksgiving verse from the New Testament seems so appropriate because of its musical connection to all these O.T. versesâ¦ ESV Colossians 3:16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, with thankfulness in your hearts to God. THE GREEK WORD FOR âTHANKSGIVINGâ IS ÎµÏÏÎ±ÏÎ¹ÏÏÎ¹Î± ( you-car-is-tee-a ). We get our English word âeucharistâ from the Greek word. âEucharistâ means thanksgiving. Studying this beautifully-sounding word yields some fascinating insights on the N.T. concept of thanksgiving. One paradoxical example is something you might be surprised to know: GIVING TO OTHERS PRODUCES THANKSGIVING IN US! THANKSGIVING, AS WE HAVE SEEN, IS COMMENDED OF BELIEVERS : âGive thanks!â Yet the Bible says that thanksgiving actually comes from God: thanksgiving is the result of grace. Thatâs interesting, donât you think? The thanksgiving we give to God comes first from God. Fascinatingâ¦ ANOTHER FASCINATING FACT IS THAT THANKSGIVING GOES ON IN HEAVEN. In other words, thanksgiving will go on forever. I think that is a great insight.
