content: The Fullness of Christ AT THE BEGINNING OF OUR STUDY I WANT TO REMIND YOU that Paulâs teaching in Ephesians 4:11-16 is one sentence in Greek, the original language of the New Testament. It is admittedly difficult to mentally grab ahold of Paulâs run-on statements and continue to hold all the way to the end of v. 16. Because of this fact, our English Bibles have divided the Greek sentence into several shorter sentences in order to attempt to keep it clear throughout. But because of the structure of the text it is easy to lose sight of the forest for the trees. Consequently, it is, I think, wise to approach vv. 13-16 a little differently than the way we have studied this passage to date, which has been generally to take a close-up look at clauses, phrases, and even words. In this particular blog I believe it is most expedient to approach Paulâs words in two steps. One step is to get an overview of the passage, which I have begun to do in these introductory words, and the second step will be to recognize points of application, trying to take Paulâs words and bring them into our own situation here at Barabbas Rd. today. â Taken in part from Garner OUR PASSAGE THIS WEEK FROM THE GREAT BOOK OF EPHESIANS DEALS WITH the building of the Body of Christ. The Body of Christ, of course, is the term the N.T. often uses to describe the Church. We might venture to say that all churches are interested in growing. We here at Barabbas Rd. are, of course, concerned with Church growth. While I would grant that all churches are interested in growing, I would add that this focus on growth â in order to be legitimate, biblical growth â must be growth in accordance with the words of the Head of the Church, the Lord Jesus Christ, as well as the words of Ephesians 4:13-16â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:13-16 until we all attain to the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature which belongs to the fulness of Christ. 14 As a result, we are no longer to be children, tossed here and there by waves, and carried about by every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, by craftiness in deceitful scheming; 15 but speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him, who is the head, even Christ, 16 from whom the whole body, being fitted and held together by that which every joint supplies, according to the proper working of each individual part, causes the growth of the body for the building up of itself in love. THIS MESSAGE ALSO DEALS WITH GROWTH, MATURITY, AND CHRISTLIKENESS. Building the Body of Christ, growth, maturity, and Christlikeness are not antithetical. You could say building the Body involves and requires growth; growth leads to maturity, which in turns leads to Christlikeness. Or you also rightly say, growth , maturity , and Christlikeness are three words that refer ultimately to the same thing, and result in the building of the Body of Christ. âTHE FULLNESS OF CHRISTâ IS REALLY ANOTHER WAY OF SAYING GROWTH , another way of saying maturity , and another way of saying Christlikeness or completeness â¦ Maturity , completeness in Christ, Christlikeness is the triangular goal of our Christian livesâ¦ NKJ 2 Corinthians 3:18 But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory , just as by the Spirit of the Lord. IN OUR LIVES RIGHT NOW, GOD IS TRANSFORMING US INTO THE IMAGE of Christ. That is what Christlikeness means. Ultimately, the Church is to be filled with souls who have been transformed into âThe Fullness of Christ.â TO EMPHASIZE THIS KEY FEATURE OF OUR PASSAGE in Ephesians 4, please look again at vv. 13-16 and Paulâs words, tis time emphasizing the clauses and phrases that emphasize growing into âThe Fullness of Christââ¦ NAS Ephesians 4:13-16 until we all attain ( attain [ ÎºÎ±ÏÎ±Î½Ïá½±Ï { ka-tan-ta-o }] means to reach, arriving at a destination, which may be seen mean to grow, mature) to the unity of the faith , and of the knowledge of the Son of God , to a mature man , to the measure of the stature which belongs to the fullness of Christ . 14 As a result, we are no longer to be children , tossed here and there by waves, and carried about by every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, by craftiness in deceitful scheming; 15 but speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him , who is the head, even Christ, 16 from whom the whole body, being fitted and held together by that which every joint supplies, according to the proper working of each individual part, causes the growth of the body for the building up of itself in love . IT IS HARD TO MISS, IS IT NOT? There are at least 5 references to growth in Christ. Clearly it is Godâs will that we are meant to grow into âThe Fullness of Christ.â âTHIS BUILDING UP OF THE REDEEMED INVOLVES A TWOFOLD ultimate objective, which Paul identifies as the âunity of the faith and âthe knowledge of the Son of God, out of which flow spiritual maturity, sound doctrine, and loving testimony.â â MacArthurâ¦ SOME SCHOLARS BELIEVE THAT PAUL HAS IN MIND HERE A FUTURE SCENARIO, but that view just doesnât seem to fit the context. âThe apostle is not describing the final work of Christ on behalf of the Church in heaven; he is talking instead about the work of gifted men in the Church on earth.â â MacArthurâ¦ THE ONLY MENTION OF THE CHURCH IN THE GOSPELS CAME FROM the mouth of Jesus Himself in Matthew 16:18â¦ NAS Matthew 16:18 âAnd I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church; and the gates of Hades shall not overpower it. SCHOLARS HAVE DEBATED FOR CENTURIES AS TO JUST WHO OR WHAT is the âthe rock.â Is the rock Jesus Himself? Is it Peter? Or is it Peterâs declaration in v. 16?â¦ NAS Matthew 16:13 -16 Now when Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi, He began asking His disciples, saying, âWho do people say that the Son of Man is?â 14 And they said, âSome say John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but still others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.â 15 He said to them, âBut who do you say that I am?â 16 And Simon Peter answered and said, âThou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.â WHATEVER THE ANSWER, ONE THING IS OBVIOUS, AND it this obvious fact that I want to stress here at the beginning of our study this week: âI WILL BUILD MY CHURCH.â IT IS JESUS, AND JESUS ALONE WHO BUILDS THE CHURCH. He works through us, yes, but it is ultimately He and He alone who is the Builder, and for that reason, the Church will ultimately, irrevocably prevail. THAT UNDERSTOOD, I WANT TO CALL OUR ATTENTION BACK TO VV. 11-12â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:11-12 And He gave some as apostles, and some as prophets, and some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers, 12 for the equipping of the saints for the work of service, to the building up of the body of Christ; LEADERS, GIFTED PEOPLE, ARE GIVEN AS GIFTS TO THE CHURCH TO SERVE and to equip and to build up. âNo community can exist without leadership of some fashion.â â Snodgrassâ¦ JESUS HAS A CLEAR AND PROGRESSIVE METHOD FOR BUILDING HIS CHURCHâ¦ NAS Ephesians 4:13 until we all attain to the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature which belongs to the fulness of Christ. âPEOPLE THAT CHRIST HAS GIFTED, LEADERS, ARE TO MINISTER TILL ALL the church attains the three goals: literally, (1) âunto the unity of the faith (cf. Eph. 4:5) and full knowledge of the Son of God, â (2) âunto a mature man,â and (3) âunto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.â As each believer functions in accord with the gift Christ has given him (v. 7) the body as a whole enjoys unity (cf. vv. 3-6) and becomes more spiritually mature (cf. v. 15), more like Jesus Christ in all His fullness (cf. 1:23; 3:19).â â Hoehner (B.K.C.) âKNOWLEDGEâIS THE GREEK WORD á¼Ïá½·Î³Î½ÏÏÎ¹Ï ( e-pi-gnow-sis ). This is an important word to Paul in Ephesians. He prayed for this knowledge fo

content: Pastor/Teacher LAST WEEK WE LOOKED AT APOSTLES, PROPHETS AND EVANGELISTS; this week we will look at pastors and teachers. âTHE ONE WHO HAS BEEN GIVEN TO THE CHURCH AS COSMIC LORD, HIMSELF gives to the Church to equip is for its cosmic task.â â Lincoln YOU MAY REMEMBER THAT IN THIS PASSAGE, which begins in v. 7, Paul is referencing an O.T. psalm. Paul is taking the imagery of Ephesians 4: 7-16 from Psalm 68, v. 18 in particular, which readsâ¦ NAS Psalm 68:18 Thou hast ascended on high, Thou hast led captive Thy captives; Thou hast received gifts among men, Even among the rebellious also, that the LORD God may dwell there . YOU SURELY NOTICED THAT IN PSALM 68:18 IT SAYS THAT GOD âRECEIVEDâ gifts, whereas in Ephesians 4 the text says, God gives gifts. As I explained before, we are not to get upset over this since it was common for N.T. writers who quoted the O.T. to do so with a freedom that enabled them to communicate their own particular purpose. You must remember that they did this through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit (it is important to keep in mind whenever we talk about the dual authorship [God and man] of the Scripture, it is incorrect to say the human writers were inspired; only the text was inspired [2 Timothy 3:16]). PAUL IS PICTURING A VICTORIOUS CHRIST, WHO FOLLOWING HIS BATTLE ON the Cross, gave gifts â think of them as spoils of battle â to individual believers. It is a beautiful and memorable image. NOTE IN V. 11 THE WORDS âHE GAVE.â ââHe gaveâ emphasizes the sovereign choice and authority given to Christ because of His perfect fulfillment of the Fatherâs will. Not only apostles and prophets but also evangelists, pastors and teachers and teachers are divinely called and placed.â â MacArthur ALTHOUGH THIS TRUTH IS SOMETIMES MISUNDERSTOOD AND ABUSED , these gifted men held âofficesâ and had âauthority.â As I mentioned last week, sadly, not all Christians recognize and respect these God-given positions and the authority that goes with them. We live in an age where it is acceptable and even applauded to resist authority. âNEVERTHELESS, THE EMPHASIS OF THIS PASSAGE DOES NOT LIE WITH the people themselves â the apostles, prophets, evangelists, and pastors and teacher as officers, but rather as gifts of Christ to His church.â â Kistemaker IT IS MY HOPE THAT YOU DO NOT MISS THAT IMPORTANT POINT. While we will be focusing on the âPastor/Teacherâ this week, we must not lose sight of the central fact that the position is not man-made but that the people who fill these positions in the Church are to be seen as Christâs gifts to the Church. AN ACCURATE UNDERSTANDING OF THIS VV. 11-12 SHOULD LEAD US not only to an appreciation of these leaders but ultimately of Christ Himself who âgaveâ these leaders as gifts to the Church. MY MAIN FOCUS THIS WEEK HAS BEEN THE QUESTION OF WHETHER PAUL IS speaking of one person or two when he says, âPastors and Teachers.â âIs it âPastors and âTeachersâ or is it âPastor/Teacherâ? This is the major difficulty of this passage. YES, I KNOW OUR ENGLISH BIBLES SEEM TO SETTLE THE QUESTION immediately. All English Bibles say âPastors and Teachers,â clearly implying that two offices, two leaders are in view. But in the Greek text of v.11 there are legitimate grammatical questions that must be answered. YOU KNOW WHAT I MEAN WHEN I SAY âGRAMMATICAL,â RIGHT? Grammar is simply rules of language. Grammar refers to the system of rules by which words are formed and put together to make sentences. By studying the grammar of a passage we are more able to determine the meaning of the passage. This is particularly necessary when studying ancient languages, such as Greek and Hebrew. IT IS INDEED A DIFFICULT QUESTION TO RESOLVE with any measurable degree of certainty. I have studied it at different times for a considerable number of years; I have read all the major commentaries on the question, and I have debated it with professors at the seminary. It is not easy to be certain. Good scholars disagree. ONE HIGHLY CREDIBLE SOURCE SAYS THIS ABOUT THE QUESTION: âSome interpreters have understood the phrase pastors and teachers to refer to one and the same group. This would mean that all pastors are teachers and that all teachers are pastors. This position is often taken because it is recognized that both nouns (i.e., pastors and teachers ) are governed by one article in Greek. But because the nouns are plural, it is extremely unlikely that they refer to the same group, but only that the author is linking them closely together. It is better to regard the pastors as a subset of teachers. In other words, all pastors are teachers, but not all teachers are pastors.â â NET Notes I WOULD SAY THAT A SLIM MAJORITY OF SCHOLARS AND KNOWLEDGABLE teachers hold this view, that Paul is not talking about a single group of leaders known as âPastor/Teacherâ but rather is speaking about two offices, two leaders: the Pastor and the Teacher. AS A GREEK PROFESSOR, I KNOW WELL THE RULES OF GREEK GRAMMAR that seem to point to that view being the correct one. There is a well-known principle in Greek grammar governing the relationship of two nouns governed by one article â the word âtheâ comes before pastors but not before teachers â both connected by the conjunction âand.â It is called the âGranville- Sharp Rule.â The Granville-Sharp rule, named after the grammarian Granville Sharp, states that it is only when the two nouns are singular can they be said to refer to the same person. For some people that settles the issue. They say that since these two nouns in view are not singular but plural â pastors and teachers â Paul cannot be referring to just one office; he has to be speaking of two. OBVIOUSLY, WE ARE IN THE TECHNICAL PART TO WHICH I REFERRED EARLIER. I TEACH THE GRANVILLE-SHARP RULE IN MY GREEK CLASSES AND I BELIEVE in its legitimacy. HOWEVER, in my view there is another issue to deal with here that is too often overlooked or casually dismissed by many, and that is that in the Greek text there is a subtle but I believe significant shift in Paulâs choice of the word âand.â Please donât let your eyes glaze over with all this technical stuff. J I am confident you can follow this with little problem and I believe you will find it worthwhile. IN GREEK THERE ARE TWO MAIN WORDS TRANSLATED âAND.â Since they are both single syllable words and easy to remember, I feel like I can use them in relating to you the issue at hand. One word is Î´á½² ( day ) and the other word is ÎºÎ±á½¶ ( kai ). Paulâs order is âapostles Î´á½² ( day ) prophets Î´á½² ( day ), evangelists Î´á½² ( day ), pastors and teachers.â But the last âandâ separating pastors and teachers is not Î´á½² ( day ), we might expect since the previous offices all were accompanied by Î´á½² ( day ). It is ÎºÎ±á½¶ ( kai ). I believe that is significant. While I understand the Granville Sharp Rule and recognize the nouns to be plural, I think that if Paul had intended to be speaking about pastors and teachers as two groups of leaders he would have used another Î´á½² ( day ) instead of changing the word and using ÎºÎ±á½¶ ( kai ). Yes, this is splitting hairs; this is dealing with rules of grammar that are sometimes arcane; but I believe it can also be seen as making an honest attempt to understand as precisely as possible Paulâs meaning using the advantage of the Greek text. I RESPECTFULLY AND HUMBLY BELIEVE THE CHANGE IN THE USE OF âANDâ is determinative. I respectfully and humbly believe that the change in the use of âandâ points to us regarding the âPastors and Teachersâ in Ephesians 4:11 as one person. âTeachersâ â of which Iâll more to say in a moment â in this context is not, I respectfully and humbly believe, pointing to another person, another office, but is explanatory of âPastors.â STAY WITH ME; WE NOT THROUGH WITH THE TECHNICAL STUFF JUST YET. content: Christâs Gifts to the Church EPHESIANS 4:11-12 THIS WEEK WE ARE GOING TO STUDY A SUBJECT THAT SHOULD greatly interest all of us who are believers in the Lord Jesus Christ. I NEED TO TELL YOU OUR PASSAGE FOR THIS WEEK IS PART OF a longer context. Verses 11-12 are part of another of the elongated sentences we find in the book of Ephesians. You will remember that vv. 3-14 back in chapter 1 comprise just one long sentence. Another extended sentence is vv.1-6 of chapter 4. And now we have another long sentence in vv. 11-16 in the Greek text. Just want to make that acknowledgementâ¦ ANOTHER THING I WOULD LIKE TO SAY IS THAT THIS PASSAGE SHOULD NOT be seen as a complete theology on how to do church. By that I mean, Paulâs words should not be seen as a paradigm for us to follow today. The most along the lines of general assessment, I believe, we can say about this passage is that it is a good foundational pattern for us to keep in mind as we do church. The passage is very valuable, to be sure, full of valuable information from a first-century perspective, but it is not an all-comprehensive, ironclad guideline. âMOST OF THE CONCERN IS FOR INTERNALLY BUILDING UP OF THE CHURCH, rather than for mission outside the church. Thus it is incomplete, but no text should be seen as a comprehensive theological statement. Aside from the 12 apostles chosen by Jesus and Paulâs special apostleship, in biblical times there were also messengers called âapostlesâ who held no extraordinary status. Our subject this week from the Word of God is one of the most controversial, most misunderstood subjects in all of the N.T. I say that sadly because it shouldnât be that way. I hope you will stay with me and think and pray through this passage with meâ¦ WE ARE GOING TO LOOK AT JUST ONE VERSE IN THIS BLOGâ¦ NAS Ephesians 4:7 But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christâs gift. ONE COMMENTATOR SAID IT THIS WAY: âthe gifts He is pleased to give.â â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ THE SUBJECT PAUL IS INTRODUCING IS SPIRITUAL GIFTSâ¦ EVERY CHRISTIAN HAS BEEN GIVEN A SPIRITUAL âGIFT OF GRACE.â And as such, we should learn about this most important giftâ¦ PAUL WROTE THESE MEMORABLE WORDS TO THE CORINTHIANS in 1 Corinthians 12:1â¦ KJV 1 Corinthians 12:1 Now concerning spiritual gifts , brethren, I would not have you ignorant. God wants us to learn about spiritual gifts. Now, knowledge alone, knowledge for the sake of itself âpuffeth upâ (1 Cor. 8:1), thatâs true. But it is equally true there is no virtue in ignorance. God wants us to constantly be learning and growing in the knowledge of His Wordâ¦ NAS Colossians 3:16 Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you, with all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with thankfulness in your hearts to God. DEFINITION, SOURCE, AND PURPOSE OF SPIRITUAL GIFTS. In this definition of spiritual gifts, you hear also both their source as well as their purposeâ¦ SPIRITUAL GIFTS ARE DIVINE ENABLEMENTS OR CAPACITIES FOR MINISTRY. They are given to believers by God in His grace to build up the church into the image of Christ its Lord. Spiritual gifts are characteristics of Jesus Christ that are to be manifested through the church just as they were exhibited through His incarnate body, just as they were through Jesus when He was on earth 2,000 years ago. In other words, each gift the Holy Spirit now gives to believers had its perfect expression in Jesusâ own life and ministry. Aside from subordination, kneeling could signify servility or worship.â â Lincolnâ¦ I have always thought it is such a beautiful thing. Because of age and injury â and lack of exercise, I might add â bowing is out the question for many, but I think we would all agree that bowing is a beautiful, appropriate posture to have before the Lordâ¦ NKJ Psalm 95:6 Oh come, let us worship and bow down; Let us kneel before the LORD our Maker. THIS SOLEMN INTRODUCTION IN V. 14 GIVES GREAT WEIGHT TO Paulâs prayer. âTwo elements make this introduction unusual: first, the reference to bowing the knee, and, secondly, the turning to one who is humbly addressed as Father and then identified as the one from whom every family in heaven and earth derives its name (v.15).â â Snodgrassâ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:15 from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name, LET ME CAUTIOUSLY DANCE ON THE RAZOR-SHARP EDGE OF POLITICS for a moment, pleaseâ¦ MAKING A POINT ABOUT PRIORITIES WHEN I PREACHED, I OFTEN SAID THAT we are Christians first and Americans second. Some eyebrows were raised, I readily admit. Nothing against patriotism within reason, I assure you. However, I stood and stand strongly behind that statement. But at the same time, I sometimes regret saying this because it can imply an exclusivity that is not biblical. Yes, we are Christians first, but we are not just Christians; we are also Americans and members of the world community. We have responsibilities to people who are not Christians. Remember, as I remind myself, every human being was created by God and bears the image of God â everyone. I found a good paragraph this week that speaks to this point; here it isâ¦ âTHE FATHE

title: The Purpose of the Mystery
excerpt: The Purpose of the Mystery EPHESIANS 3:8-13 DOES ANYONE REMEMBER WHAT âTHE MYSTERYâ WAS? First of all, what is a mystery?â¦ A BIBLICAL MYSTERY IS SOMETHING THAT HAS NOT BEEN PREVIOUSLY revealedâ¦ âThe secret things of Godâ¦
content: The Purpose of the Mystery EPHESIANS 3:8-13 DOES ANYONE REMEMBER WHAT âTHE MYSTERYâ WAS? First of all, what is a mystery?â¦ A BIBLICAL MYSTERY IS SOMETHING THAT HAS NOT BEEN PREVIOUSLY revealedâ¦ âThe secret things of God are the mysteries that God knows about life and about the future which humanity desperately needs to know.â â Steadmanâ¦ Scripturally speaking, the mystery would have remained a mystery had not it been supernaturally revealedâ¦ âOBVIOUSLY THE MYSTERY TO WHICH PAUL REFERS HERE IS THAT OF JEW and Gentile being one in Christ, about which he wrote before in brief in chapter 1:9-12 and chapter 2:11-12. It was unknowable, incomprehensible truth hidden from all men until revealed by God.â â MacArthurâ¦ THE MYSTERY OF CHAPTER 3 OF EPHESIANS WAS THAT in Christ Jew and Gentile believers became one in Godâs sight and members of His kingdom and family. From last weekâs blog hereâs what Paul said in v. 6â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:6 to be specific , that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel, NOW LOOK AT V. 4â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:4 And by referring to this, when you read you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, âIT WAS PAULâS INTENTION NOT SIMPLY TO DECLARE THE MYSTERY BUT TO explain and clarify it. When Ephesian believers and every subsequent believer including us would read his explanations, Paulâs hope was that they would come to understand his God-given insight into the mystery of Christ.â â MacArthur/TARâ¦ NOW LETâS LOOK AT OUR PASSAGE FOR THIS WEEK: Ephesians 3, vv. 8-13â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:8-13 To me, the very least of all saints, this grace was given, to preach to the Gentiles the unfathomable riches of Christ, 9 and to bring to light what is the administration of the mystery which for ages has been hidden in God, who created all things; 10 in order that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known through the church to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenly places . 11 This was in accordance with the eternal purpose which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord, 12 in whom we have boldness and confident access through faith in Him. 13 Therefore I ask you not to lose heart at my tribulations on your behalf, for they are your glory. âTHIS TEXT IS HIGHLY PERSONAL AND FOCUSED ON Paulâs first-century responsibility. At first glance some may conclude this text is not too relevant for us and consequently we should hurry on to the next passage. This is unfortunate, for while Paulâs call and the revelation to the apostles and prophets cannot be duplicated, the theologies embedded in these verses are important for our lives.â â Snodgrassâ¦ WE ALL SHOULD APPROACH EVERY PASSAGE IN GODâS WORD WITH a real sense of expectancy. Whatever the sermon title or subject matter, we all should expect to receive something of value to our lives. The reason I can say this is that Godâs Word is a living Word; it is spiritually alive and valuable to our lives today. That is such an important fact for us to remember. People who miss Sunday sermons â to some degree at least â miss what God is say to them through their Pastor in this unique context. I know, some will argue, âbut I read my Bible at home,â or âbut I go to a weekly Bible study.â Let me lovingly but firmly say, itâs not the sameâ¦ SOME SCHOLARS SEE V. 7 AS BELONGING TO THIS PASSAGE AND NOT the previous passage. Verse 7 readsâ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:7 of which I was made a minister, according to the gift of Godâs grace which was given to me according to the working of His power. VERSE 7 IS WHAT WE CALL A âTRANSITION VERSE,â in that it could be seen as either ending the passage begun in v. 1 of chapter 3 or the introduction to the following passage, our passage for this week. Studiously, prayerfully, I chose to see v. 7 as concluding the previous passage, vv. 1-7â¦ VERSE 7 HARMONIOUSLY BLENDS INTO V. 8, AS PAUL IS HUMBLY SPEAKING OF his personal ministry as the âApostle to the Gentilesââ¦ NAS Romans 11:13 But I am speaking to you who are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I magnify my ministry, âPAUL IS NOT SAYING IN V. 3 THAT HE ALONE IS A STEWARD OF GODâS SECRETS. All Christians are stewards of Godâs mysteries. You are and so am I. We have received the gospel, the story that explains all of life and enables us to solve the riddle of our existence. This responsibility was committed to us by God, and He expects us to dispense this secret to those around us.â â Steadmanâ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:8 To me, the very least of all saints, this grace was given, to preach to the Gentiles the unfathomable riches of Christ, âUNFATHOMABLEâ CAN BE A HARD WORD TO SAY, BUT it is a most accurate word in describing the riches of Christ. âChristâs fathomless spiritual wealth can never be fully comprehended.â â Hoehnerâ¦ THE GREEK WORD USED HERE IS FOUND ONLY ONE OTHER PLACE IN THE N.T.â¦ NAS Romans 11:33 Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and unfathomable His ways! THE GREEK WORD á¼Î½ÎµÎ¾Î¹ÏÎ½á½·Î±ÏÏÎ¿Ï ( a-nex-ik-nee-as-tos ) literally means ânot to be tracked out,â ânot capable of being traced by footprintsâ; inscrutable, incomprehensible. I see God and His blessings to me that way â donât you?â¦ NAS Romans 11:33 â¦ How unsearchable are His judgments and unfathomable His ways! BACK TO EPHESIANS 3:8â¦ Arenât those especially beautiful words from a humble man? I have heard more than a few people in my life as a pastor and teacher â especially women â comment to me that they thought Paul was an arrogant man. Nothing could be further from the truth. Paul was a very humble person. Listen to what he said of himself in 1 Corinthians 15:9â¦ NAS 1 Corinthians 15:9 For I am the least of the apostles, who am not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God. âPAUL WAS HUMBLED BY THE PRIVILEGES GOD HAD GIVEN TO HIM BECAUSE he sincerely viewed himself as the least of all the saints. In v. 8, Paul expressed himself with a sudden outburst of amazement that God would use him to proclaim the Lord Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior.â â Garner/TARâ¦ âTHEN OR NOW, THE MAN WHO IS GENUINELY CALLED BY GOD IS in constant danger of losing his effectiveness by coming to think of himself as more than a servant. When he loses his sense of servanthood, at that same time he loses his spiritual power and usefulness. When he exalts himself and begins to work in his own human power and according to his own plans, he competes with God and forfeits his spiritual power.â âMacArthurâ¦ IN A CULTURE THAT SO HIGHLY PRIZES INDEPENDENCE, CONSIDER these wordsâ¦ âTo lose dependence is to lose everything, because everything that is of any value in our lives as Christians, including power for service, comes only from the Lord.â â MacArthurâ¦ WITHOUT LIFTING MYSELF UP AT ALL, I FEEL EXACTLY LIKE PAUL. I was an intellectual, artistic, worldly-minded, philosophic blasphemer raising my family arrogantly and shamefully apart from God. And now, amazingly through Godâs grace, I was given the unspeakable privilege of preaching and teaching Godâs Word. Every day without fail, I thank God for the miracle He has brought about in my life. Praise His holy nameâ¦ PAUL GOES ONTO SAY IN V. 9â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:9 and to bring to light what is the administration of the mystery which for ages has been hidden in God, who created all things; IN VV. 8-9, PAUL WAS GIVEN THE GRACE âTO PREACH TO THE GENTILES the unsearchable riches of Christâ and âto make plain to everyone the administration of this mystery.â He considered it a great privilege and he never grew tired of exercising that deep privilegeâ¦ âPAUL WAS TO DISCLOSE PUBLICLY TO EVERYONE, NOT JUST the Ephesians (cf. Eph. 3:2) this stewardship of Godâs sacred secret (vv. 3-4, 6). This secret had been hidden in God (cf. v.5), the Creator of the universe. Even before creating all things God had in mind this wonderful truth as part of His eternal plan (cf. 1:4, 11).â â Ho

title: The Revelation of Mystery
excerpt: The Revelation of Mystery EPHESIANS 3:1-7 NAS Ephesians 3:1-7 For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentilesâ 2 if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of Godâs grace which wasâ¦
content: The Revelation of Mystery EPHESIANS 3:1-7 NAS Ephesians 3:1-7 For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentilesâ 2 if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of Godâs grace which was given to me for you; 3 that by revelation there was made known to me the mystery, as I wrote before in brief. 4 And by referring to this, when you read you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, 5 which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit; 6 to be specific , that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel, 7 of which I was made a minister, according to the gift of Godâs grace which was given to me according to the working of His power. IâVE TITLED THIS BLOG , âThe Revelation of the Mysteryââ¦ âFOR THIS REASONâ CONNECTS THIS PASSAGE WITH OUR PASSAGE FROM LAST week: âThe Foundation and the Cornerstone.â Explaining Paulâs opening words is a little technical, so please bear with me at the start here. letâs look again at vv.19-22 of chapter 2â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:19-22 So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and are of Godâs household, 20 having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the corner stone , 21 in whom the whole building, being fitted together is growing into a holy temple in the Lord; 22 in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling of God in the Spirit. BUT TO BETTER UNDERSTAND PAULâS BEGINNING THIS PASSAGE WITH âFor this reason,â we must go to v. 13 of chapter 3â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:13 Therefore I ask you not to lose heart at my tribulations on your behalf, for they are your glory. SCHOLARS TELL US THAT âFOR THIS REASONâ AND THE REST OF V. 1 AND V. 13 are to be understood as parentheses around everything in between. So, our passage for this week more accurate would be labeled vv. 2-7. As I said, itâs a little confusing, but I want us to try to understand. âThis is the way the apostleâs active mind often worked. He often started out to say one thing, but then he is captured by the truth of something else he is going to say, so he pours this second truth into a grand parenthetical clause which he builds, truth upon truth, until he finally returns to his original thought and completes the statement he began in v. 1. Understanding how vv. 1 and 13 connect gives us a context for understanding what Paul is saying in the intervening sentences.â âSteadmanâ¦ VERSE 14 OF CHAPTER 3 BEGINS A PRAYER OF PAULâSâ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:14 For this reason, I bow my knees before the Father, SEE HOW HE PICKS UP WITH âFOR THIS REASONâ AGAIN? Just as Paul began his prayer in v. 1, he thinks of something important and gives us vv. 2-13 before continuing his prayer in v. 14. This is just how the amazingly fertile mind of Paul worked at timesâ¦ SO OUR PASSAGE TODAY AND OUR NEXT STUDY ARE ACTUALLY A âsubstantial digressionâ (Bruce) from a prayer uttered by Paul on behalf of the Christians in Ephesus, which youâll remember is modern Turkey in Asia Minorâ¦ âTHE APOSTLE WANTED THE CHRISTIANS TO WHOM HE WAS WRITING TO understand why he was going through persecution and imprisonment. Paul, youâll also remember, was writing from prison, most probably in Rome. Ephesians is one of what are termed âthe Prison Epistlesâ of Paul. Paul, again most probably, wrote the letter to the Ephesians from a rented room where he lived under house arrest, chained day and night to a Roman soldier. Paulâs Christian friends must surely have wondered how God could allow this great missionary to be confined in this way, his missionary voice shut up within four walls, his missionary feet in chains, reduced to conducting his ministry by letters alone.â â Steadman/TARâ¦ YES, BUT WHAT POWERFUL LETTERS THEY WERE, AND ARE STILL TODAYâ¦ PAUL SAYS IN V. 1â¦ NAS Ephesians 3:1 For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentilesâ âTHE SUBJECT âI PAULâ IS LEFT WITHOUT A VERB. The main verb does not come until v. Whenever Paul uses the expression âI Paul,â as he does several times in his letters, the phrase denotes special emphasis. In 2 Corinthians 10:1 and Galatians 5:2, for example, âI Paulâ introduces a solemn entreaty or warning.â â Bruceâ¦ NAS 2 Corinthians 10:1 Now I, Paul, myself urge you by the meekness and gentleness of Christâ I who am meek when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent! NAS Galatians 5:2 Behold I, Paul, say to you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to you. IN EPHESIANS 3:1, PAUL WAS CALLING ATTENTION TO THE FACT that he was in prison because of his special ministry to the Gentiles. Paul, remember, was the âApostle to the Gentiles.â In Romans 11:13, it says thisâ¦ NAS Romans 11:13 But I am speaking to you who are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I magnify my ministry, PAUL WAS IN PRISON IN GREAT PART BECAUSE OF THE GENTILESâ¦ NOW LETâS GO BACK TO VV. 2 AND 3 AND PICK UP OUR STUDY FOR TODAY of the mysteryâ¦ NAS Ephesians 3:2-3 if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of Godâs grace which was given to me for you; 3 that by revelation there was made known to me the mystery, as I wrote before in brief. WITH THESE WORDS PAUL IS EMPHASIZING HIS DIVINELY GRANTED authority for the teaching he about to giveâ¦ â STEWARDSHIPâ IS FROM A GREEK WORD (Î¿á¼°ÎºÎ¿Î½Î¿Î¼á½·Î± [ oi-ka-no-me- a]), a word that primarily referred to the management of a household. âA steward was responsible for taking care of that which belonged to someone else.â â Macarthurâ¦ PAUL, WE COULD SAY, WAS TAKING CARE OF GODâS GRACE; he was a steward of Godâs grace to the Gentilesâ¦ âPAUL IS NOT SAYING IN V. 3 THAT HE ALONE IS A STEWARD OF GODâS SECRETS. All Christians are stewards of Godâs mysteries. You are and so am I. We have received the gospel, the story that explains all of life and enables us to solve the riddle of our existence. This responsibility was committed to us by God, and He expects us to dispense this secret to those around us.â â Steadmanâ¦ GOD GIVES EVERY BELIEVER A SPIRITUAL GIFT. This special gift really doesnât belong to us, however; it was given us by God. We are to take care of that gift, nurture that gift, and use that gift in ministry to othersâ¦ NAS 1 Peter 4:10 As each one has received a special gift, employ it in serving one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. MOST CHRISTIANS I KNOW BELIEVE THEY HAVE MORE THAN ONE GIFT, BUT Peter says we have only one gift. In the Greek text the relevant words are singular. You may have many talents, and you may be using those talents in a number of ministries in the church, but I believe the Bible teaches that we only have one special gift, and as Peter tells us, that gift is to be used in serving one anotherâ¦ NOTE IN V. 2 THAT THIS GRACE WAS GIVEN TO PAUL FOR THE GENTILES. âPaul did not choose either his apostleship or his ministry; he was appointed.â âMacArthurâ¦ LISTEN TO WHAT PAUL SAID REGARDING THIS POINT IN 1 TIMOTHY 1:12â¦ NAS 1 Timothy 1:12 I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, because He considered me faithful, putting me into service; THERE IS APPLICATION FOR US TODAY HERE. So often it is we ourselves who choose our ministries. If we be faithful and obedient, and God will give us a ministryâ¦ NOW NOTICE IN V. 3 THAT IT WAS BY REVELATION THAT THE MYSTERY WAS revealed to Paulâ¦ A MYSTERY IS SOMETHING THAT HAS NOT BEEN PREVIOUSLY REVEALED. âThe secret things of God are the mysteries that God knows about life and about the future which humanity desperately needs to know.â â Steadmanâ¦ Scripturally speaking, the mystery would have remained a mystery had not it been supernaturally revealedâ¦ âOBVIOUSLY THE MYSTERY TO WHICH PAUL REFERS HERE IS THAT OF JEW and Gentile being one in Christ, about which he wrote before in brief in chapter 1:9â12 and

title: The Foundation and the Cornerstone
excerpt: The Foundation and the Cornerstone EPHESIANS 2:19-22 IN THIS WEEKâS BLOG, VV. 19-22 OF CHAPTER 2 PROVIDE A SUMMARY conclusion to the passage we have been studying for the past couple of weeks, namely the union of bothâ¦
content: The Foundation and the Cornerstone EPHESIANS 2:19-22 IN THIS WEEKâS BLOG, VV. 19-22 OF CHAPTER 2 PROVIDE A SUMMARY conclusion to the passage we have been studying for the past couple of weeks, namely the union of both Jewish believers in Christ and Gentile believers in Christ into one body, the Church. Gentiles, youâll remember, are all peoples who are not Jewsâ¦ THIS UNION, AS WE HAVE LEARNED, WAS MADE POSSIBLE ONLY THROUGH THE sacrifice of the Lord Jesus on the Cross. Jesus is the peace that brought the two hostile groups together. Look again with me at our passage from last weekâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:14-18 For He Himself is our peace, who made both groups into one, and broke down the barrier of the dividing wall, 15 by abolishing in His flesh the enmity, which is the Law of commandments contained in ordinances, that in Himself He might make the two into one new man, thus establishing peace, 16 and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, by it having put to death the enmity. 17 And He came and preached peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near; 18 for through Him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father. PAUL IS TELLING HIS READERS IN VV. 11-22 THAT the plight of alienation from God, which both the Jew and Gentile experienced before the Cross, is overcome by Godâs grace and the gracious privilege of life with Godâ¦ OUR PASSAGE FOR THIS WEEK IS EPHESIANS 2:19-22â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:19-22 So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and are of Godâs household, 20 having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the corner stone , 21 in whom the whole building, being fitted together is growing into a holy temple in the Lord; 22 in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling of God in the Spirit. âPAUL CLOSES HIS DISCUSSION OF THE MARVELOUS UNITY OF THE BODY of Christ by giving three metaphors (examples, word pictures â TAR) to illustrate it. In the picture of fellow citizens he shows how Jew and Gentile have become part of the same kingdom. In the picture of Godâs household he shows how all believers are one spiritual family in Christ. And thirdly, in the picture of a holy temple in the Lord Paul shows that all believers are together a habitation for God.ââ MacArthurâ¦ IN OUR PASSAGE, JEWISH AND GENTILE BELIEVERS ARE PICTURED by Paul as (1) fellow citizens, (2) members of Godâs household, and (3) living stones of a holy temple. Look again at v. 19â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:19 So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and are of Godâs household, THE âYOUâ IN V. 19 IS REFERRING TO GENTILE BELIEVERS. Because of Christâs sacrifice, these Gentile believers are no longer strangers and aliens, far off from God, but are now fellow citizens with the saints. The saints are the universal Church, all the believers throughout history. âThese Gentile believers become a part of the company of the redeemed of all ages beginning with Adam.â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ BUT IT IS VERY IMPORTANT WE UNDERSTAND THAT PAUL IS NOT SAYING THAT the church has become one with Israel. While there are many similarities between the two bodies, they have always been distinct, and are distinct today. Neither is Paul saying that the church inherits the blessings promised to Israelâ¦ THERE ARE THREE REASONS THIS IS NOT SO: â(1) In the context Paul was discussing the âone new man.ââ â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:15 by abolishing in His flesh the enmity, which is the Law of commandments contained in ordinances, that in Himself He might make the two into one new man, thus establishing peace, IN V. 16, PAUL REFERS TO THIS AS âONE NEW BODYââ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:16 and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, by it having put to death the enmity. âENMITYâ IS HOSTILITYâ¦ WHILE SOME MAY MISTAKENLY TAKE PAULâS WORDS TO MEAN THAT the Church and the Nation of Israel are now the same, this is not so. âPaul does not mean that Gentiles are incorporated into Israel. He is, however, saying that believing Jews and Gentiles are now incorporated into one new âhumanity.ââ â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ I REALIZE THIS MAY BE CONFUSING FOR SOME TO UNDERSTAND, BUT because this is such an important point, bear with me as I try to explain this to youâ¦ WHILE JEWS AND GENTILES WHO BELIEVE IN CHRIST DO INDEED become united into one body of believers, that is, the Church, nevertheless, the distinction between the Church and the Nation of Israel remains intactâ¦ THE CHURCH IS NOT ISRAEL, AND ISRAEL IS NOT THE CHURCH. The two entities have never been the same; they are not the same today; and they will not be the same in the future. Even though Jews who believe in Christ and Gentiles who believe in Christ become fellow citizens in the kingdom of Godâ¦ LET ME SAY THE SAME THING ANOTHER WAY. While both the individual Jew and the individual Gentile who believe in Christ become one in the body of Christ, the corporate bodies of Israel and the Church do not become oneâ¦ THE SECOND REASON THAT PAUL IS NOT SAYING THAT THE CHURCH AND Israel have become the same entity is â(2) Paul specifically stated that Gentiles are incorporated âwith Godâs peopleâ and are in âGodâs householdâ(v. 19); he did not use the word âIsrael.ââ â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:19 So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and are of Godâs household, âIF PAUL MEANT THAT THE CHURCH HAD BECOME ISRAEL, HE WOULD HAVE named both groups, as he did in verse 11.â â Hoehner (B.K.C)â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:11 Therefore remember, that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called âUncircumcision â by the so-called âCircumcisionââ¦ (The Gentiles are the âuncircumcisonâ and the Jews are the âCircumcisionâ)â¦ NOW LOOK AT V. 20â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:20 having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the corner stone , âTHE LANGUAGE IN VV. 20-22 SHIFTS WITHOUT WARNING FROM speaking of a family to describing a building, which is then defined more narrowly as a temple. There is a fascinating wordplay in the Greek text, which we will not explore due to time and space, that facilitates this abrupt change.â â Snodgrassâ¦ SCHOLARS DIFFER SOMEWHAT AS TO THE EXACT MEANING OF THE PHRASE âthe foundation of the apostles and prophets.â It is my opinion after studying the various views that the meaning is not that the apostles and prophets themselves are the foundation (the genitive is probably subjective, not objective â TAR), but rather, the phrase âthe apostles and prophetsâ refers to their teaching, âthe divine revelation that they taught, which in its written form is the New Testament.â âMacArthurâ¦ âTHE TEACHING OF THE APOSTLES AND PROPHETS IS THE BASIS ON WHICH the Church rests.â â Snodgrassâ¦ THE TEACHING, AS YOU MIGHT EXPECT, POINTS TO CHRISTâ¦ Jesus is the subject and goal of the teachingâ¦ NAS Colossians 2:6-7 As you therefore have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him, 7 having been firmly rooted and now being built up in Him and established in your faith, just as you were instructed, and overflowing with gratitude. STILL, I MUST CONFESS THAT I COULD BE WRONG. I acknowledge that a strong case can be made for the phrase âthe apostles and prophetsâ referring not to their teaching but to them themselves. Listen to these words from a well-respected conservative scholar: âThe words could be translated, âthe foundation which consists of the apostles and prophets.â This makes the best sense when one sees in 4:11 that the apostles and prophets were gifted men given to the church as its âfoundation.ââ â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ NAS Ephesians 4:11-12 And He gave some as apostles, and some as prophets, and some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers, 12 for the equipping of the saints for the work of service, to the building up of the body of Christ; âFURTHERMORE,â THIS SCHOLAR GOES

title: Our Peace
excerpt: Our Peace EPHESIANS 2:14-18 BECAUSE THIS BLOG IS A CONTINUATION of last weekâs message, âBrought Near by the Blood,â a good place to begin would be to read the verses we studied last weekâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:11-13â¦
content: Our Peace EPHESIANS 2:14-18 BECAUSE THIS BLOG IS A CONTINUATION of last weekâs message, âBrought Near by the Blood,â a good place to begin would be to read the verses we studied last weekâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:11-13 Therefore remember, that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called âUncircumcisionâ by the so-called âCircumcision,â which is performed in the flesh by human handsâ 12 remember that you were at that time separate from Christ, excluded from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. 13 But now in Christ Jesus you who formerly were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. YOU WILL REMEMBER THAT THIS PASSAGE DECLARED THAT through the blood of the Lord Jesus, Jew and Gentile believers in Christ, two historically, culturally, and religiously hostile groups of people were reconciled in one body â the Body of Christ, the Church. The sacrificial death of the Jesus on the Cross made this miraculous reality possibleâ¦ âMIRACULOUSâ IS NOT AN EXAGGERATION. The Jews despised the Gentiles because they considered themselves better than Gentiles. âWe have the Law of Moses,â they said. âThe Law is right and true; it reflects the character of God. You Gentiles donât have the Law.â And in their self- righteous arrogance, they thought they were keeping the Law because they didnât do some of the outward, external acts the Law prohibited. And so they hated and despised the Gentiles because they thought they were superior. The Gentiles, on the other hand, hated the Jews, for their smugness and hypocrisy. So there was intense hostility between them.â â Steadmanâ¦ THE CHURCH IS A MIRACLEâ¦ âTHE SINS OF BOTH JEWS AND GENTILES CAN BE FORGIVEN BECAUSE OF His death, and both can be brought near to each other. Divisions are overcome, not by an approaching or a receiving on either side, but by Christ coming and making peace for both.â â Foulkesâ¦ PAUL WROTE THESE RELEVANT WORDS IN COLOSSIANS 1:20â¦ NAS Colossians 1:20 and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, having made peace through the blood of His cross; through Him, I say , whether things on earth or things in heaven. NOT ONLY CAN IT BE CORRECTLY SAID THAT CHRIST BRINGS PEACE, it is also true that He is âOur Peaceââ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:14-18 For He Himself is our peace, who made both groups into one, and broke down the barrier of the dividing wall, 15 by abolishing in His flesh the enmity, which is the Law of commandments contained in ordinances, that in Himself He might make the two into one new man, thus establishing peace, 16 and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, by it having put to death the enmity. 17 And He came and preached peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near; 18 for through Him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father. THERE IS AN IMPORTANT EMPHASIS AT THE BEGINNING OF V. 14 THAT we must not overlook. It is particularly emphatic in the Greek textâ¦ âFOR HE HIMSELF IS OUR PEACEââ¦ The âforâ connects v. 14 with our passage from last week, but note especially the âHimself.â This is emphatic: âHe Himself,â or it could also be translated âHe alone.â In the Greek text the pronoun (Î±ÏÏÎ¿Ï [ au-tos ]) from which we get the word âHimselfâ comes first in the sentence. First place in a sentence in Greek indicates special emphasisâ¦ âHE HIMSELF IS OUR PEACE,â that is, what everything else â whether the law with its ordinances, human merit, law-works of whatever kind, sacrifices, etc. â could not do, He, He alone in His own person, has done, for He is the very embodiment of peace. In His capacity as the Prince of Peace He, by means of His voluntary sacrifice, has brought about peace, reconciliation not only between God and man, but also between Gentile (the âuncircumcisionâ) and Jew (the âcircumcision.â)â Hendriksen/Kistemakerâ¦ YOU WILL REMEMBER THAT THE PROPHET ISAIAH, writing some 700 years before the birth of Jesus, foretold that one of the titles of the coming Messiah would be âThe Prince of Peaceââ¦ NAS Isaiah 9:6 For a child will be born to us, a son will be given to us; And the government will rest on His shoulders; And His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace. âTO SAY THAT JESUS IS OUR PEACE SETS FORTH MORE EMPHATICALLY the truth than to say, as Paul does in v. 15, âmade peaceâ or in v. 17 âproclaimed peace.â â Bruceâ¦ Paul in v. 14 could not be more emphaticâ Jesus Christ Himself is our peace!â¦ WHILE THE FOCUS OF THE PASSAGE â THIS WEEK, LAST WEEK, AND next week â is rightly on the peace between Jews and Gentiles, when the entire context is considered, as well as the remainder of the book, Paul is actually making a threefold classification: Jew, Gentile (Greeks), and the Christian, the Church of God. âNo wonder that Christians in the first century spoke of themselves as a âthird raceâ or ânew race,â no longer Jewish, no longer Gentile.â â Bruceâ¦ IN 1 CORINTHIANS 10:32, PAUL SAID JUST THISâ¦ NAS 1 Corinthians 10:32 Give no offense either to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God; THE WORD âPEACEâ IS FOUND 359 TIMES IN THE BIBLE (according to BibleWorks)â¦ I STUDIED THE MEANING OF THE WORD âPEACEâ ALL WEEK from a variety of sources and I believe I can say to you with confidence that the biblical definition of peace is very probably the definition you have in your minds right now. In other words, while both the Hebrew and Greek words for peace have numerous shades of meaning and must be evaluated according to their context, our English understanding of peace is very likely accurateâ¦ LISTEN TO THESE DESCRIPTIVE WORDS OF PEACE AND SEE IF THEY DO NOT agree with the images you are now mentally experiencing about peace. First the descriptive words that reflect the O.T. Hebrew concept of peace: soundness, completeness, security, welfare , and absence of conflict . Descriptive words coming mainly from the N.T. Greek concept of peace: harmony, concord, security, safety , and assurance â¦ HEREâS A DEFINITION OF âPEACEâ FROM A POPULAR BIBLE DICTIONARY : Peace : Total well-being, prosperity, and security associated with Godâs presence among His people. Linked in the OT with the covenant, the presence of peace, as Godâs gift, was conditional upon Israelâs obedience. In prophetic material, true peace is part of the end-time hope of Godâs salvation. In the NT, this longed-for peace is understood as having come in Christ and able to be experienced by faith.â Baker Theological Dictionaryâ¦ THE HEBREW WORD FOR âPEACEâ IS ××Ö¹××© ( sha-lome )â¦ My Hebrew N.T. says that âHe is our ××Ö¹××© (sha-lome ). You have doubtless heard of this word and know it to mean peace . That is correct. However, the exact meaning of the word is difficult to state. Aside from peace , it can mean hello and also goodbye ; it can mean health , financial prosperity , wholeness , and completeness . Ultimately ××Ö¹××© ( sha-lome ) is a general idea with an extremely wide circle of associated meanings in almost all its occurrences, it has something of a vague, enigmatic character, all goodâ¦ I THINK WE CAN ALL AGREE THAT OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE WORD âpeaceâ is all good. âPeaceâ is not a negative word. It is a beautiful word, a positive word, and a powerful word, especially when it is understood in terms of its relationship to Jesusâ¦ NAS Romans 5:1 Therefore having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, NAS Romans 8:6 For the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace, NAS Romans 15:33 Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen. NAS Romans 16:20 And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you. PAULâS USUAL GREETINGS IN HIS LETTERS TO THE FIRST-CENTURY CHURCHES in the N.T. often included the word âpeace.â Here are just three examplesâ¦ NAS 2 Corinthians 1:2 Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. title: Brought Near By the Blood
excerpt: Brought Near By the Blood EPHESIANS 2:11-13 OUR PASSAGE THIS WEEK MAY NOT BE ON THE SAME EXALTED LEVEL AS a number of our recent passages from Ephesians have been. Ephesians 2:11-13 may indeed not be a âBeethoven 5thââ¦
content: Brought Near By the Blood EPHESIANS 2:11-13 OUR PASSAGE THIS WEEK MAY NOT BE ON THE SAME EXALTED LEVEL AS a number of our recent passages from Ephesians have been. Ephesians 2:11-13 may indeed not be a âBeethoven 5thâ passage but, as I think you will see, it is nevertheless miraculousâ¦ THE BRINGING TOGETHER OF THE JEW AND THE GENTILE IN CHRIST â when all circumstances are considered â is indeed miraculousâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:11-13 Therefore remember, that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called âUncircumcision â by the so-called âCircumcision,â which is performed in the flesh by human handsâ 12 remember that you were at that time separate from Christ, excluded from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world. 13 But now in Christ Jesus you who formerly were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ TO FULLY APPRECIATE THE WONDER OF THIS PASSAGE WE MUST REMIND ourselves of the traditional and long-standing animosity between the Jews and the Gentiles of the first century. Quite simply, the Jews hated anyone who was not a Jew. And in turn, the Gentiles despised, envied, and feared the Jews. Think of Gentile as meaning non-Jew in this context; the Jew might term the Gentile a pagan , or even a dog . Ask either a Jew or a Gentile if he could ever foresee a union between the two distinct cultures, and the answer would surely have been something along the lines of âImpossible!â or âNever!ââ¦ ONE COMMENTATOR TITLED THIS PASSAGE âSTRANGERS IN DARKNESS.â Another commentator called this passage âStatement of the Union,â the union between Jew and Gentile, a union that is accomplished only in Christ. No other being, no other force, could ever accomplish such a seeming impossibilityâ¦ IT WOULD BE SIMILAR TO GOD BRINGING MUSLIMS AND JEWS TOGETHER TODAY. Impossible! It will never happen!â¦ âBEFORE THE EPHESIANS TRUSTED CHRIST, THEY HAD BEEN ALIENATED from God. They were dead to Him and much alive to sin.â â Garnerâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:1-3 And you (Gentiles) were dead in your trespasses and sins, 2 in which you formerly walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, of the spirit that is now working in the sons of disobedience. 3 Among them we too (Jews) all formerly lived in the lusts of our flesh, indulging the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest. HOWEVER, GOD HAD SAVED THEM BY HIS GRACE THROUGH THEIR FAITHââ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8-9 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; 9 not as a result of works, that no one should boast. THROUGH THE SUPERNATURAL POWER OF GRACE â Godâs undeserved favor â God had brought both Gentile and Jew into right relationship with Him. âBefore they had become believers, Jews and Gentiles had lived in hostility to one another. Godâs saving grace also changed all of those seemingly permanent negative relationships.â â Garnerâ¦ âTHIS UNION OF JEWISH AND NON-JEWISH BELIEVERS INTO ONE BODY FORMS the basis for Paulâs discussion for the rest of the book of Ephesians.â â Hoehner/TARâ¦ THE GENTILES WERE THE ONES CALLED âUNCIRCUMCISIONâ AND THE JEWS were the ones Paul calls âCircumcision.â As you probably know, the sign of the covenant, the distinguishing mark, for the Jew was circumcisionâ¦ NAS Genesis 17:10 âThis is My covenant, which you shall keep, between Me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised. âCIRCUMCISION, AS IâM SURE YOU KNOW, IS THE SURGICAL REMOVAL OF the foreskin from the male sex organ. Circumcision is very important in the Scriptures. It is referred to throughout both the Old and New Testaments. The practice began with Abraham, who circumcised his son Isaac at Godâs command.â â Steadmanâ¦ NAS Genesis 21:4 Then Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him. âTHIS CIRCUMCISION SIGNIFIED A SPECIAL RELATIONSHIP TO GOD. The Gentiles did not circumcise. The Jews are the circumcised people. Circumcision marked the Jews as a special people, uniquely belong to God. â â Steadmanâ¦ âTHIS PHYSICAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN JEWS AND GENTILES affected every area of their lives. A great social and spiritual boundary existed between them.â â Hoehner (B.K.C.)â¦ âWHY DO YOU THINK GOD WOULD CHOOSE THIS PARTICULAR PART of the body as a sign that the Jewish people were specially chosen by God? The answer is that our sexuality is a basic part of our humanity. The Scriptures teach this very plainly. The church has often been squeamish about teaching the plain biblical truth of our sexuality. But sex and sexuality are not unmentionable to God MIRACULOUSLY, THESE TWO SEEMINGLY DIFFERENT CULTURES â which when properly understood include the whole world â were âBrought Near by the Bloodââ¦ The blood of Christ shed for the salvation of all who would come to Him by faith is the unifying factor for the entire worldâ¦ NAS Galatians 3:28 There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. âTHE BIBLE CALLS THE GENTILE, PAGAN WORLD âUNCIRCUMCISEDâ BECAUSE it was characterized by two elements: Sexual immorality and religious ignorance. Like the pagans in our own society, many of the pagans in Paulâs day were highly educated â what we would call âcivilized.â But, also just like America and the world today, mingled with their civilization was a terrible sexual degeneracy. When you visit the ancient ruins of the pagan would â like the ancient temples of Greece and Rome â you find a tremendous emphasis on sex symbols. Homosexuality was widespread and widely accepted, along with other degrading, unnatural sexual practices. So the pagan world of Paulâs day revealed its lack of understanding and respect for its own humanity by its degraded sexual practices.â â Steadmanâ¦ NO, THIS LITTLE PASSAGE MAY NOT SEEM AS DRAMATIC AS SOME of the miracles Christ performed in His earthly ministry, but when all factors are considered, bringing these two opposing cultures together in one faith was a supernatural event that could only be described as miraculousâ¦ âIN CHRIST, THE EPHESIAN BELIEVERS, BOTH JEWS AND GENTILES, HAD BECOME a family of faith. Paul called then to remember the former great divide, a social and spiritual gulf so wide, so deep, that only God could bridge it.â â Garnerâ¦ SALVATION IS ALL OF GODâ¦ âWHAT WAS PAULâS PURPOSE IN WRITING THIS PASSAGE under the Holy Spiritâs inspiration? Was it simply to encourage or was there something more, something else in his heart? Yes, he wrote to encourage the Ephesians, it is difficult to see this as his only motivation. Paul was overwhelmed with awe as he witnessed Godâs mighty power at work. The living God had created something altogether new in the universe. God had reconciled both Gentiles and Jews into one body through the cross of Christ. That amazing unity is the result of divine creative power!â â Garner/TARâ¦ AND PAUL WANTED THEM ALL TO âREMEMBERâ THIS. The verb form (imperative) in the Greek text is in the present tense, which denotes continuance and which may imply that the Gentiles were to continue to remember their former plight of their desperate situation of being separate from Godâ¦ ALTHOUGH THE JEWISH BELIEVERS IN CHRIST HAD AT ONE TIME ALSO BEEN separated from God, the Gentiles were worse off. âGod had given Israel the revelation of the O.T. along with certain privileges which the Gentiles did not have.â â Hoehnerâ¦ NAS Romans 9:4 who are Israelites, to whom belongs the adoption as sons and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the Law and the temple service and the promises, NAS Ephesians 2:11-12 Therefore remember, that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called âUncircumcision â by the so-called âCircumcision,â which is performed in the flesh by human hands- 12 remember that you were at that time sepa

excerpt: Good Works THIS WEEKâS BLOG IS A CONTINUATION FROM OUR PREVIOUS MESSAGE IN Ephesians, âSaved by Grace,â vv. 8-9â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8-10 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is theâ¦
content: Good Works THIS WEEKâS BLOG IS A CONTINUATION FROM OUR PREVIOUS MESSAGE IN Ephesians, âSaved by Grace,â vv. 8-9â¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8-10 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; 9 not as a result of works, that no one should boast. 10 For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. âGODâS SALVATION HAS ALREADY IN EPHESIANS BEEN DESCRIBED IN TERMS OF a resurrection from the dead, a liberation from slavery, and a rescue from condemnation. Now it is spoken of as a new creation, and a further reason ( for; cf. v. 8) is given why this salvation is not of human origin and therefore cannot be the basis for human boasting. It is Godâs workmanship from first to last; believers have been created in Christ Jesus for good works. These good works cannot be the ground of our salvation or the subject of our boasting since they are the goal of the new creation. They are the fruit of salvation, not its basis or cause. So once again in this magnificent paragraph the apostle makes clear that we are wholly dependent on Gods gracious, sovereign activity for our salvation.â â OâBrien, Pillar Commentary â¦ GOOD WORKS WILL NEVER GET A PERSON SAVED, BUT once saved, good works are to be the goal of every Christianâ¦ âTHE WORK OF GRACE WHICH HAS TRANSFORMED THOSE WHO WERE spiritually and morally dead into new men and women, alive with the resurrection life of Christ, is Godâs work from first to last.â â Bruceâ¦ THE BIBLE TELLS US THAT WE ARE GODâS âWORKMANSHIPâ â a fascinating word as you will soon see â created by God in Christ Jesus for âGood Worksââ¦ âWE ARE HIS WORKMANSHIP.â âThe term rendered workmanship , which often appears in the LXX to denote creation as Gods work, has the same nuance of the physical creation in its only other New Testament occurrence (Rom. 1:20). But here in Ephesians 2:10, which stresses what believers are because of God, the cluster of creation terms, including this word and created , along with good works , is applied directly to the new creation. â OâBrienâ¦ NAS Romans 1:20 For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made , so that they are without excuse. âGODâS INVISIBLE NATURE IS PERCEIVED WITH THE MINDâS EYE BY THE THINGS God has created.â â BDAG Lexicon . If human beings can only perceive God through the things He has created, and we are things He created, what does that tell you? We are Godâs creations that He has made so that others can perceive God! That is a monumental insight and a monumental responsibility, is it not?â¦ WE WERE MADE BY GOD FOR THE PURPOSES OF GODâ¦ THE WORD âMADEâ HERE, AND THE WORD âWORKMANSHIPâ IN Ephesians 2:10, both are from the Greek word ÏÎ¿Î¯Î·Î¼Î± ( poi-a-ma ), which means, that which is made, work, creation. [BDAG]. Interestingly, this is the Greek word from which we get the English word poem . While not all scholars agree, I believe it is accurate to think of ourselves as âPoems of God.â Poems are things that are made by an artist. We are things that are made by Godâ¦ AND AS YOU SURELY KNOW, BELIEVERS ARE CALLED in the Bible ânew creationsââ¦ NAS 2 Corinthians 5:17 Therefore if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things passed away; behold, new things have come. OUR PASSAGE TELLS US THAT WE ARE CREATED BY GOD, the same supernatural way as the creation of the worldâ¦ âPAUL GOES ON TO TELL US IN V. 15 OF CHAPTER 2 OF EPHESIANS THAT Gods purpose was to create one new humanity out of Jews and Gentilesâ â OâBrienâ¦ NKJ Ephesians 2:14-15 For He Himself is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of separation, 15 having abolished in His flesh the enmity, that is , the law of commandments contained in ordinances, so as to create in Himself one new man from the two, thus making peace, AND NOTICE WHAT PAUL SAYS IN GALATIANS 6:15â¦ NAS Galatians 6:15 For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation. WEâLL LOOK CLOSER AT THIS NEW HUMANITY IN TWO WEEKSâ¦ APART FROM CLEARLY GLORIFYING GOD AS the sole author of our salvation, v. 10 also places a great privilege and responsibility upon usâ¦ WE WHO ARE PART OF GODâS NEW CREATION ARE CALLED UPON TO LIVE IN a way befitting our lofty position. Thatâs heavy. Listen to what Paul says in chapter 4, v. 1â¦ NKJ Ephesians 4:1 I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you to walk worthy of the calling with which you were called, IT IS QUITE POSSIBLE THAT THIS IMPORTANT MANDATE IS the most overlooked, casually rationalized aspect of our salvation. I trust you will agree with me when I say this is to our collective shameâ¦ PAUL SAID BACK IN CHAPTER 1â¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, THE EXPRESSION âIN CHRISTâ AND ITS VARIATIONS IS FOUND SOME 11 TIMES in chapter 1â¦ AND HERE IN 2:10, WE SEE ANOTHER REFERENCE OF âIN CHRISTââ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:10 For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. IT IS SO COMFORTING TO KNOW THAT WE AS BELIEVERS ARE âIN CHRISTââ¦ âTHERE ARE IMPORTANT ETHICAL CONSEQUENCES OF BEING CREATED IN CHRIST Jesus. The divine intention, forcefully expressed by the purpose clause, is that we should walk in good deeds. We have a responsibility to live in the world so as to please him. There was a time when we walked in disobedience and sin, followed the ways of this world , were in terrible bondage to the devil, and were destined for wrath. But now because of Godâs mighty salvation in which a glorious change has been effected, we are expected, through the agency of his Holy Spirit, to demonstrate a changed life- style. Our attitudes and behavior are to show all the hallmarks of the new creation. And when we walk in these ways which are according to his purpose, it is he himself who is powerfully working in our lives.â â OâBrienâ¦ NAS Philippians 2:12-16 So then, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your salvation with fear and trembling; 13 for it is God who is at work in you, both to will and to work for His good pleasure. 14 Do all things without grumbling or disputing; 15 that you may prove yourselves to be blameless and innocent, children of God above reproach in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you appear as lights in the world, 16 holding fast the word of lifeâ¦ WE WERE CREATED IN CHRIST JESUS âFORâ GOOD WORKS. Like so many others, e.g., âin,â and âbut,â here is another little word that tells us so muchâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:10 For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. THIS LITTLE WORD âFORâ TELLS US OUR PURPOSEâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:10 For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works , which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. âCHRIST JESUS IS THE âSPHEREâ OF GODâS NEW CREATION.â â OâBrianâ¦ âTHE BIBLE HAS MUCH TO SAY ABOUT WORKS. It speaks of the works of the Law, which are good but cannot save a person (Gal 2:16). It speaks of the dead works (Heb 6:1) and of works, or deeds, of darkness and of the flesh, all of which are inherently evil (Rom 13:12; Gal 5:19-21; Eph 5:11). All of those works are done in manâs own strength and have nothing to do with salvation.â â MacArthurâ¦ âALTHOUGH THEY HAVE NO PART IN GAINING SALVATION, GOOD WORKS have a great deal to do with living out salvation. No good works can produce salvation, but many good works are produced by salvation. When Godâs people do good deeds they bear fruit for His kingdom and bring glory to His name.â â MacArthurâ¦ NAS John 15:8 âBy this is My Father glorified, that you bear much fruit, and so pro
