content: The Gift of God THE FIRST CHAPTER OF EPHESIANS TAUGHT US of our exalted position in Christâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, CHAPTER 2, AMONG OTHER THINGS, TEACHES US clearly about our past, our present, and, as we will see in the coming weeks, our future. Verse 1 of chapter 2 tells us of our pastâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:1 And you were dead in your trespasses and sins, VERSES 4-5 TELL US WHO WE ARE NOWâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:4-5 But God, being rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, 5 even when we were dead in our transgressions, made us alive together with Christâ¦ OUR PASSAGE THIS WEEK WILL TELL US HOW GOD TRANSFORMED US in salvationâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8-9 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; 9 not as a result of works, that no one should boast. GOD SAVED US BY GRACEâ¦ OUR SALVATION IS âTHE GIFT OF GODââ¦ IT IS ESSENTIAL WE KNOW AND REMEMBER THAT WE ARE SAVED BY GRACE. The fact that we are saved by grace and not our own good works should forever change and dominate our perspective on lifeâ¦ âTHE WAY YOU SEE YOUR LIFE, SHAPES YOUR LIFEâ¦â â Rick Warren ( I am not an avid fan of Rick Warren, but I think this is a good quote; I believe this is true. )â¦ CERTAINLY MOST OF YOU HAVE HEARD MORE THAN ONE SERMON ON the grand, fundamental subject of Godâs grace, e.g., Grace is Godâs unmerited favor, undeserved kindness. But I urge you to consider this blog on grace with new interest. Grace is bigger than a one-sentence definition, even one as deep and comprehensive as this familiar oneâ¦ ONE OF THE BIGGEST RESPONSIBILITIES OF A PASTOR/TEACHER IS to remind. Accordingly, the apostle Peter saidâ¦ NAS 2 Peter 1:12 Therefore, I shall always be ready to remind you of these things, even though you already know them , and have been established in the truth which is present with you . ALLOW ME TO REMIND YOU THIS WEEK OF âTHE GIFT OF GODâ that we have been given. Even though I believe you know this, I am going to purposely be repetitious in stating this the fact that our salvation is âThe Gift of Godâ in order to most effectively emphasize this most important reminder. I hope youâll stay with meâ¦ BACK IN THE RECENT DAY ON MOST COMPUTERS THERE WAS A âREFRESHâ BUTTON. When you hit the âRefreshâ icon on your screen it instantly straightened the files and documents that were on your desktop. The Bible is like that ârefreshâ capacity. The Word of God is a living Book, deep and multi-dimensional beyond our imagination, totally capable of renewing itself in wonderful ways in our present lives. Along with me I urge you to hit the ârefreshâ button on your mental computers during this blog and allow Godâs Word to straighten up your spiritual desktop â in other wordsâ¦ REVIEWâ¦ âLOVEââ¦ WHILE THE WORD IS NOT MENTIONED IN OUR PASSAGE this week, I would like to plant that great word firmly in our minds as we begin our study. The love of God is the major theme behind all other themes in this towering epistle. The love of God is the foundation of the doctrine of salvationâ¦ NAS John 3:16 âFor God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish, but have eternal life. GOD LOVES YOU. I donât think most people review this most prominent fact enough. Over the years in counseling people as a pastor and teacher it is my observation that people generally make things harder on themselves, make their burdens heavier by failing to refresh that button in their minds. Allow me to repeat these incredible words with emphasis: GOD LOVES YOU! I think you will agree with me those three words have the power to instantly and amazingly transform our minds regardless of circumstance. The circumstance may remain hard and heavy but weâll be different and better in facing themâ¦ GOD LOVES YOU! I urge you to receive and believe those words. I have learned to discipline myself to remind myself that God loves me throughout each day. The practice doesnât make me reckless or irresponsible but gives me a confidence to face any situation. I believe doing this can be proven to be essential to your health â not just your spiritual health, but your mental health and even your physical health as well. If we do not believe with our innermost being that God loves us, we are cutting ourselves off from most all that is good and wise and powerful. But if we live our lives secure in the knowledge that God loves us, we are empowered to live victoriously above all circumstances in Christâ¦ IâM NOT GETTING OFF TRACK FROM EPEHESIANS 2:8-9 ; I would argue that Godâs love is really the focus of this passage. What is grace but an expression of His love? Whatâs more, Godâs love is the focus of the entire Book of Ephesians, and the focus of the entire Bibleâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; FIRST OF ALL, PLEASE NOTE THE LITTLE WORD âFOR.â It is connecting v. 8 with v. 7; it is âproviding support for Paulâs stress on the surpassing richness of Godâs grace to believers in v. 7.â â Lincolnâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:7 in order that in the ages to come He might show the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. IT PLEASES GOD TO DEMONSTRATE THE RICHES OF THE GRACE He has lovingly bestowed upon usâ¦ âVERSE 8 IS REPEATING, EXPANDING, AND EXPOUNDING the parenthetical statement made in v. 5.â â rewritten slightly from Foulkes. This repeating, expanding, and expounding is Paulâs way of making this awesome statement in v. 8 even more emphaticâ¦ âHOW CAN THE LIFE OF HEAVEN BE POSSESSED HERE AND NOW? How is there such an exhibition of the love of God from which the whole creation of God can learn and wonder? Because by grace you have been saved.â â Foulkesâ¦ WE ARE SAVED BY GRACE â SAVED FROM WHAT? The opening v. of chapter 2 tells us the answer clearlyâ¦ NIV Ephesians 2:1 As for you, you were dead in your transgressions and sins, WE HAVE BEEN SAVED BY GRACE FROM OUR SINSâ¦ HERE IS A MODERN DYNAMIC TRANSLATION OF V. 1â¦ NLT Ephesians 2:1 Once you were dead, doomed forever because of your many sins. WE WERE SPIRITUALLY DEAD BEFORE WE ARE SAVED. If we do not fully grasp this fact we are unlikely to give God the credit he deserves in our salvation. We were dead! Itâs in your Bible. Dead people canât save themselves. God took the initiativeâ¦ GOD SAVED US FROM SPIRITUAL DEATH, OUR FROM TRESPASSES AND SINSâ¦ NAS Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. NAS Ephesians 2:4 But God, being rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, âBECAUSE OF HIS ABUNDANT MERCY AND GREAT LOVEâ God made us alive together with Christââ¦ WHAT AMAZING LOVE IS THIS ! Because of His great love God saved people that were under His wrath, worldly, fleshly, sinnersâ¦ âTHE GIFT OF GODââ¦ THIS BLOG IS ALL ABOUT HELPING US COMPREHEND OUR POSITION in Christâ¦ NAS Ephesians 2:8 For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; COULD IT BE ANY CLEARER? We are saved by graceâ¦ WITHOUT GETTING TOO TECHNICAL, ALLOW ME TO GIVE YOU THE LITERAL translation of the words âyou have been saved by grace.â The verbal idea here is expressed by a perfect passive participle {a periphrastic construction}, which is literally translated, âyou are having been saved.â The idea expressed by the Greek verbal construction is that you have been saved as a completed act in the past and that the results of that completed act are ongoing. âHave been savedâ is a passive idea, which means you didnât save yourself; you were saved by Someone else. All in all, this verbal construction strongly supports doctrinal position of Barabbas Rd. Church and most other conservative Biblical churches, in that it clearly expresses the fact that God takes the initiative

excerpt: Praying with Power EPHESIANS 1:15-23 HAVING CONCLUDED PAULâS LENGTHY AND AWESOME INTRODUCTION , the apostle concludes chapter 1 with a lengthy and awesome prayer in vv.15-23. As youâll remember, Paulâs introductionâ¦
content: Praying with Power EPHESIANS 1:15-23 HAVING CONCLUDED PAULâS LENGTHY AND AWESOME INTRODUCTION , the apostle concludes chapter 1 with a lengthy and awesome prayer in vv.15-23. As youâll remember, Paulâs introduction comprised the longest sentence in the entire Bible: 12 verses in the Greek text. Well, we go from one long sentence to another; Paulâs prayer is the second longest sentence in the Bible: 9 verses in the Greek textâ¦ BECAUSE IT IS ONE UNINTERRUPTED PRAYER AND BECAUSE , unlike the introduction, it has one central subject, that is, prayer, we will study the whole prayer in this blogâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:15-16 For this reason I too, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which exists among you, and your love for all the saints, 16 do not cease giving thanks for you, while making mention of you in my prayers; âWITH EPHESIANS 1:15, WE LEAVE THE GREAT DOCTRINAL PASSAGE in which the apostle Paul teaches the fundamental principles of the Christian faith. We are turning now to the issue of prayer and the crucial place prayer has in the Christian experience.â âSteadmanâ¦ âTHIS PASSAGE IS ABOUT PAULâS PRAYER FOR HIS READERS. The emphasis is on having the spiritual insight to understand better the immeasurable extent of Godâs plan and Godâs power. The lesson of this passage encourages us to seek a better understanding of Godâs plan and power.â â Garnerâ¦ âPRAYING WITH POWERââ¦ I wonder how many Christians actually think of their prayers as being powerful? I have often told my students this relevant thought: âThe ancient Jews thought of Prayer as a Mighty Weapon; why should we consider it any less?ââ¦ PRAYER IS POWERFULâ¦ ONE WRITER TITLED THIS PASSAGE âOUR RESOURCES IN CHRIST.â Another commentator titled vv. 15-23 âThanksgiving and Prayer,â another âPaulâs Powerful Prayer for Spiritual Insight.â It is a passage filled with beautiful concepts which teach and reassure us as believers todayâ¦ âFOR THIS REASONâ (the Holman Christian translation has âThis is whyâ) in v. 15 probably refers to Paulâs entire introduction, though some scholars suggest it may be referring only to vv.13-14âBecause of the many spiritual benefits God has given the Ephesians, including the facts that they had been redeemed, forgiven, adopted, and sealed with the Holy Spirit, Paul had good reason to give thanks and to pray for them to receive greater spiritual insight.â â Garnerâ¦ PAUL SAYS THAT HE HAD HEARD OF THE EPHESIANSâ FAITH AND LOVE . Letâs all consider that point for a moment. He didnât say that he had heard of the new carpet they had installed in their meeting place. He didnât say he had heard of their new cooling and heating system, of their state of the art sound system, of their promotional banners, or even of their childrenâs programs, or their annual church picnic, as wonderful and honoring to God they might be. He said he had heard of their faith and love. Faith and love marked the Ephesians. Faith and love should mark all Christiansâ¦ âFAITH AND LOVE MUST BE KEPT IN BALANCE. Many monks, hermits, and countless others throughout the history of the church have endeavored to keep their faith pure but have not reached out to others in love as the Lord commands every believer to do.â â MacArthurâ¦ NAS John 15:10, 12 âIf you keep My commandments, you will abide in My love; just as I have kept My Fatherâs commandments, and abide in His love. â¦ 12 âThis is My commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you. âTOO MANY CHRISTIANS TODAY BECOME HERESY HUNTERS. In other words they are eager to tear down what is wrong. The church is full of legalistic, self-righteous people like this, people are quick to tell you what is wrong. Thatâs sad. But even sadder is these people seldom do anything to build up what is good. They are full of criticism but deficient in love.â â MacArthur/TARâ¦ PAUL SAID IN ROMANS 12â¦ NAS Romans 12:10 Be devoted to one another in brotherly love; give preference to one another in honor; AND JOHN SAID IN 1 JOHNâ¦ NAS 1 John 3:18 Little children, let us not love with word or with tongue, but in deed and truth. NKJ 1 John 5:2 By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep His commandments. âFAITH AND LOVE DEFINE THE CHARACTER OF THE CHURCH, and both need to be present for the church to be what Christ wants it to be. However theologically correct a churchâs belief is, however noble its worship, however happy its fellowship or stirring its music, a church is not what it needs to be unless faith and love pervade its life and ministry.â â Garnerâ¦ THE EPHESIANS HAD FAITH AND LOVE IN BALANCE , and Paul in his prayer thanked God for themâ¦ HE SAID IN V. 16â¦ NAS Ephesians 1:16 do not cease giving thanks for you, while making mention of you in my prayers; âOBVIOUSLY, PAUL DID NOT MEAN that he gave thanks and prayed around the clock for the Ephesian believers. Rather he meant that he prayed often and faithfully for them. Paul consistently and unweariedly prayed for other people.â â Garner IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO IGNORE THE FACT THAT PAULâS PRAYER FOCUSES on othersâ¦ This fact is easily conformed by a brief look at the first chapters of some of his other letters in the N.T. Let me give you three examplesâ¦ NAS Philippians 1:3-4 I thank my God in all my remembrance of you, 4 always offering prayer with joy in my every prayer for you all, NAS Colossians 1:3 We (Paul and Timothy) give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you, NAS 2 Timothy 1:3 I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience the way my forefathers did, as I constantly remember you in my prayers night and day, WHEN YOU PRAY FOR OTHERS, YOU TAKE YOUR FOCUS OFF OF YOURSELF for a moment. Thatâs good; thatâs healthy; thatâs Christ likeâ¦ WHEN YOU PRAY FOR OTHERS, DO YOU REGULARLY THANK GOD FOR THEM? I must confess to you that for years I was lax on this. I think I can say that throughout my walk with the Lord I have always faithfully prayed for others, but I was not in the habit of thanking God for my loved ones. I am happy to say that thanking God for my loved ones is now a regular part of my prayers. I thank God everyday for my dear wife, for my daughters and their husbands and my grandchildren, and for Pastors Matt and Paul and Brett and Rob, and you here at Barabbas Rd.â¦ I BELIEVE THERE IS A GOOD LESSON FOR US RIGHT HERE in these first verses. We cannot help but notice that the focus of Paulâs prayer is on others, and not only that but notice what he prayed forâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:17 that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give to you a spirit of wisdom and of revelation in the knowledge of Him. NOTICE HERE THAT PAUL PRAYS TO GOD THE FATHER . I believe the Bible repeatedly, directly and indirectly, that our prayers are to be addressed to God the Father. When the disciples asked Jesus how they should pray He told them to address their prayers to God the Fatherâ¦ NAS Matthew 6:9 âPray, then, in this way: âOur Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be Thy name. WE ARE TO PRAY TO THE FATHER IN THE NAME OF THE SON BY THE POWER of the Spirit. Certainly, we are not dishonoring to the Father when occasionally we address Jesus or the Holy Spirit in our prayers, but basically, generally we are instructed by Godâs Word to pray to the Fatherâ¦ GOD THE FATHER IS âTHE FATHER OF GLORY.â What a beautiful way to address God, donât you agree? Many Greek scholars see this as better interpreted âthe glorious Fatherâ (attributive genitive), though I respectfully believe it should be retained as âthe Father of Glory.â ââThe Father of gloryâ is a Semitic (genitival) phrase that carries the force of the O.T. notion of glory as the mode of Godâs being and activity. âGloryâ denotes the splendor of the divine presence and power.â â Lincolnâ¦ âWISDOM AND REVELATIONââ¦ The Greek word for ârevelationâ (á¼ÏÎ¿Îºá½±Î»ÏÏÎ¹Ï [ a-pa-ka- loop-sis ]) is, youâll surely remember from Pastor Mattâs sermons, the word from which the last book in the Bible takes its name: âRevelation.â

title: New Testament Books
excerpt: New Testament Books â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego Pastor Paul of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego teaches about the books of the New Testament in this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video. Learning about theâ¦
content: New Testament Books â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego Pastor Paul of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego teaches about the books of the New Testament in this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video. Learning about the number of books, the different types of books, and the placement of the books in the New Testament can help to better understand the Bible. The Bible is comprised of 66 books total. The Old Testament contains 39 of them, and the New Testament has 27 books total. The Old Testament was originally written in Hebrew, and the New Testament was originally written in Greek. A great place to start when learning about the books of the New Testament is to open the Bible to the Table of Contents page. This helpful page can be used anytime you are searching for a specific book, perhaps during worship at your church in San Diego or elsewhere or during your own personal study. The books of the New Testament are divided into four categories: Gospels, history, letters, and Revelation. The books are not necessarily placed in the New Testament in chronological order, but in a way that is organizational. The Gospels are the first four books of the New Testament: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. The first three are called the Synoptic Gospels because they share very similar stories and information between the three of them. The writings in John are quite different, but all four focus on Jesus and his life and ministry. The next category is history. The books of Acts fulfills this category because it contains historical record of the formation and doings of the early Christian Church. The third category is letters, or the epistles. Many of these letters were written during the happenings recorded in the book of Acts. They were authored by the Apostle Paul, as well as Peter, James, and others. Revelation is the final category and is the only book in this category. The book of Revelation was authored by John and tells of things to come. It is a futuristic book. Here are a few tips on searching for books in the New Testament. All of the books that begin with the letter âTâ â 1 and 2 Thessalonians, 1 and 2 Timothy, and Titus are all right next to each other. Some of the biggest letters, like Romans and 1 and 2 Corinthians, are found at the beginning of the letters category. The four Gospels come first and Revelation is at the very end. These few guidelines can help make New Testament book searching easier. You can watch the whole Whiteboad Wednesday video below.

excerpt: Sealed With the Spirit EPHESIANS 1:13-17 NAS Ephesians 1:13-14 In Him, you also, after listening to the message of truth, the gospel of your salvationâ having also believed, you were sealed in Him with the Holy Spiritâ¦
content: Sealed With the Spirit EPHESIANS 1:13-17 NAS Ephesians 1:13-14 In Him, you also, after listening to the message of truth, the gospel of your salvationâ having also believed, you were sealed in Him with the Holy Spirit of promise, 14 who is given as a pledge of our inheritance, with a view to the redemption of Godâs own possession, to the praise of His glory. IN THIS WEEKâS BLOG, WE WILL COMPLETE PAULâS INTRODUCTION to his letter to the Ephesians. You will remember from earlier studies that, following his greeting, the apostle, employs a specific form of praise rooted in Jewish worship (called the berakah ) to introduce his theme in the letter with one long sentence. In the Greek text, vv. 3-14 comprise one uninterrupted sentence, the longest sentence in the entire Bibleâ¦ A JEWISH âBERAKAHâ IS AN EXTENDED BLESSING : the Hebrew phrase ( ba-rook a-tah a-do-nai ): Blessed art Thou, O Lord! Such outbursts of praise in various forms are found throughout the Jewish O.T. Here are a couple of examplesâ¦ NAS Psalm 103:1 A Psalm of David . Bless the LORD, O my soul; And all that is within me, bless His holy name. NAS Psalm 34:1 A Psalm of David when he feigned madness before Abimelech, who drove him away and he departed . I Will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. NAS Psalm 134:1 A Song of Ascents . Behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD, Who serve by night in the house of the LORD! For example, an English dictionary I have on my computer says that an inheritance is a : (materially) the act of inheriting property b : (immaterially) the reception of genetic qualities by transmission from parent to offspring c : the acquisition of a possession, condition, or trait from past generationsâ¦ 3 a : TRADITION b : a valuable possession that is a common heritage from history. I believe you will find there is real comfort in the meditative understanding of this excellent message from Godâs Wordâ¦ THIS IS A MESSAGE ABOUT THE FUTUREâ¦ âWHEN PAUL WROTE EPHESIANS, HE WAS UNDER HOUSE ARREST and constant guard in Rome. Even so, his heart and mind looked to the horizon and beyond it to Godâs planned future in Christ. Consider how close are our horizons most of the time; how shortsighted and petty our daily concerns usually are! â¦Let us turn our near focus and look at our lives and the future with Paulâs perspective to an eternity when the here and now will pass away and Christ will unite us under His mighty and glorious rule.â â Garnerâ¦ DURING THIS TIME IN GODâS INCOMPARABLE WORD, MAYBE WE CAN TRY TO adjust our usual human focus on self and our earthly perspective, and try to see things as we really should see them, through the lens of Scripture and the sure promises contained therein. title: Marriage Imagery in Eschatology
excerpt: Marriage Imagery in Eschatology â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego explains how Jewish marriage imagery is utilized toâ¦
content: Marriage Imagery in Eschatology â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego explains how Jewish marriage imagery is utilized to describe the end times in the Bible. A topic that has been taught at his church in San Diego before, Matt depicts the process of a traditional Jewish wedding and how it is reflected in scripture to capture the image of the last days and the end of the world. A traditional Jewish wedding began with a betrothal, or agreement, between two families. When a man was betrothed to a woman, he was legally married to her. However, the two people did not consummate their marriage at that time. Up to a year went by before the husband and wife came together as one flesh in sexual union. During this waiting period, the husband would prepare a place for his wife â a home for them. The wife would maintain her virginity in order not to dishonor her father, her family, and her husband. When the husband finished his work, he would take his wife and bring her to the new home, often in the middle of the night or at an unknown time. Then the two would finally consummate their marriage. Then came the time for celebration. The whole family would process through town and invite friends and townspeople they met along the way to join them in a marriage celebration feast. This grand party could last up to a week long and would be very festive. This very same idea is captured in scripture when referring to Jesus, the church, and the end of the world. Jesus is the bridegroom and the church is the bride of Christ, made pure before him. Israel is a friend of the bridegroom, welcomed to join in on the wedding feast of the Lamb. Just as the bridegroom prepared a place for his new wife, Jesus is preparing a place for his bride in heaven. This beautiful promise was presented to the disciples when Jesus was sharing the Last Supper with them in the upper room. In the end, the church will be taken to heaven by God and tribulation on earth will follow. At the end of this great trial, Jesus will return with His holy ones to completely overtake the earth and bring the believers into the millennial kingdom, where they too will partake in the marriage celebration. content: Resurrection MARK 16:1-8 âTHE BODILY RESURRECTION OF JESUS CHRIST FROM THE DEAD IS the crowning proof of Christianity. Everything else that was said or done by the apostles is secondary in importance to the resurrection. If the resurrection did not take place, then Christianity is a false religion. If it did take place, then Christ is God, and the Christian faith is absolute truth.â (Henry M. Morris) â¦ WE WILL BE LOOKING AT MARKâS ACCOUNT OF THE RESURRECTION: Mark 16:1-8. Mark does not give us all the details the other gospel writers do. And in Markâs brevity we find, I think, a certain poetic beauty. Mark may at times perplex us with his lack of details, but at the same time, I believe, we find ourselves swept away by the power of his unadorned phrasing. I think the key to appreciation in the book of Mark is to focus on what is said and donât allow your mind to get sidetracked by speculating about what is not said. That is probably a good rule for all of our study of the Bible, and, I might humbly suggest, maybe even all of lifeâ¦ âREJOICE, ALL YE PEOPLE, your mighty anthems raise; The Savior victorious, is worthy of your praise. All glorious Lord, Thy triumphs we proclaim, Who from the grave has risen, O praise His name!â âALLELUIA! ALLELUIA! Hearts to heaven and voices raise; Sing to God a hymn of gladness, Sing to God a hymn of praise. He who on the cross as Savior For the worldâs salvation bled, Jesus Christ, the King of Glory, Now is risen from the dead.â PEOPLE HAVE ASKED THROUGHOUT THE AGES , âDid the Resurrection really happen?â âThe body of Jesus was taken from the Cross and, in accordance with Jewish burial customs, was wrapped in a lined cloth. As much as 100 pounds of aromatic spices, mixed together to form a gummy substance, were applied to the wrappings of cloth about the body. Then the body was placed in a solid rock tomb. An extremely large stone weighing as much as 2 tons was rolled by means of levers against the entrance of the tomb. A Roman guard of strictly disciplined men was stationed to guard the tomb. If anyone tampered with the tomb or if somehow someone were allowed to take the body, the Roman soldiers would pay for it with their lives. title: Dispensational Timeline
excerpt: Dispensational Timeline â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video presentation, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses the dispensational timeline asâ¦
content: Dispensational Timeline â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video presentation, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses the dispensational timeline as represented by the Bible. This topic, something that has been taught at his church in San Diego many times, gives clarity to Godâs overall timeline. The main point of this timelines manifests that God is working with two different people groups: Israel, and the Church. Israel is distinct in that it is a nation of people, and the Church is distinct in that it is a body of people. The two entities are found in the dispensational timeline of the Bible. From the book of Genesis all the way through to Acts chapter 2 in the New Testament, the timeline focuses on the nation of Israel. They were Godâs chosen people, created and cared for by him, and for whom He sent Jesus to save them from sin and death. Then from Acts chapter 2 until Revelation chapter 3, the Bible focuses on the formation and the setting of the early Christian Church. The book of Acts is all about the actions of the Holy Spirit to bring people to faith and to grow the Christian Church. Then in Revelation chapter 3 through the end of the book, God is talking about the nation of Israel again and how they will be saved through Him. These three main sections, focusing on two distinct groups, make up the dispensational timeline of the Bible. If the timeline only focused on Israel and the section from Acts chapter 2through Revelation chapter 3 did not exist, then the Bible would make sense for the Jewish people and for their faith. However, God is doing something unique in the Bible. He is covering all people â including the Christian Church â to be the recipients of His bountiful promises and covenants. These blessings are meant not just for the nation of Israel, but for all people who put their trust and faith in God. Understanding the dispensational timeline a little better can facilitate an easier studying of the Bible. It can shed clearer light as to where and how certain things fit in the timeline. title: Lent, Biblical or Not?
excerpt: Lent, Biblical or Not? â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses the church practice of Lent and whether or not it is aâ¦
content: Lent, Biblical or Not? â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses the church practice of Lent and whether or not it is a Biblical practice. Some Christian denominations, like Catholics and some Protestant churches, practice Lent each year as a part of the church-year cycle. Many churches, however, like Barabbas Road Church in San Diego, do not participate in this practice. Either way, Lent is not right or wrong, but it is unnecessary. The season of Lent begins on Ash Wednesday and concludes with Easter. Its origins were noble: it was designated to be a time of repentance and self-reflection. Other early Christian practices had noble origins, too, such as the Sabbath. God ordained the Sabbath as a holy day for the Israelites. For the early Christian Church, however, the Sabbath became an âidolâ day. The same idea holds true for Lent. In Catholicism, Lent became a sacramental practice; that is, it was a means of grace for people. The practice of Lent infused â or injected â grace into a person. The Bible, however, says that the only mediator of grace is Jesus Christ. Through His death on the cross for the sins of the world, grace is imputed instantly. A person receives grace immediately upon belief in Christ. That being said, a person is free to practice Lent or to not participate in it at all. The goal of Lent is noble but it is not necessary. In Colossians 2, the apostle Paul speaks to a church body that was interested in practicing special days and setting up traditions. Paul communicates to the people that no one can judge them for participating in their designated special days and traditions. Therefore, no one can say that Lent is wrong. However, Paul continues by saying that as Christians, we have died to the elemental material things of this world and are made new in Christ. Knowing this, why would we submit to regulation? Verse 23 says that these regulations âhave an appearance of self-made religionâ that offer no benefit to a person. Instead of focusing on earthly traditions, Christians should seek things above that are from God. Do let Lent be a distraction that keeps you from reading Godâs Word and seeking God in all things. title: Freedom from Pornography

content: Freedom from Pornography â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego This âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video focuses on fighting and overcoming an addiction to pornography. Pastor Paul from Barabbas Road Church in San Diego casts light on the tempting nature of porn and the steps that can be taken to overcome it. Pornography, by definition, is any explicit content in the form of an image, text, story, writing, or audio recording. Greek in origin, the word pornography literally means âsexually immoral writings.â 1 Thessalonians 4:3 says that the will of God is that we abstain from sexual immorality; therefore, the Bible refutes pornography. It is not acceptable in Godâs eyes, yet it is a temptation that can be overcome with Godâs help. Three factors contribute to a porn addiction: accessibility, accountability, and appetite. Accessibility and appetite must be removed and accountability must be arranged in order for someone to conquer an addiction to pornography. First, any form of accessibility to porn must be eliminated. An access point could be a computer, phone, or printed material. If someone is truly intent on beating a porn addiction, all access points must be completely and totally removed. This could even mean using a basic phone â one that does not have internet access â and giving up a smart phone, for example. Take any extreme measure necessary. Second, an addicted person must find accountability. Being accountable means intentionally and openly communicating with someone about struggling with pornography. Here is where the body of Christ, like Christian friends or your local church body such as Barabbas Road Church in San Diego, can be of crucial assistance. Pastors and church leaders are accountable resources, too. They are not sin free and do not think of themselves more highly than others. Even after someone has adopted excellent accountability partners, action must still be taken by that person to intently fight the addiction and completely remove it from life. Third, an addicted person must stop feeding the porn-hungry appetite. Instead, that person should focus on feeding the spirit. This means being proactive in feeding the soul instead of giving in to the temptation to feed the desire for pornography. Get radical and remove any possible outlet that may satisfy the appetite. Pray consistently, read Godâs Word frequently, and be on guard. Reach for God â He alone offers hope and grace to help overcome any level of temptation or addiction. You can watch the whole Whiteboad Wednesday video below.

content: Predestination THIS WEEK IN OUR ONGOING STUDY OF THE GREAT BOOK OF EPHESIANS, we will once again be facing a very difficult subject: the subject of âPredestination.â And once again I must get technical in many of my comments. I donât apologize for this. I remind you, we are dealing with the deepest of all doctrines of the Bible as we seek as much as humanly possible to plum the very mind of God. Aside from the 8th chapter of Romans, there is no chapter in the Bible that is deeper than chapter 1 of the book of Ephesiansâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3-6 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, 4 just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him. In love 5 He predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the kind intention of His will, 6 to the praise of the glory of His grace, which He freely bestowed on us in the Beloved. YOU WILL NOTE THAT THE WORD âPREDESTINEDâ IS A VERBAL FORM, NOT a noun. It is important to note this: the noun âpredestinationâ is not found in Scripture. Therefore, the subject of âPredestinationâ is one that is classified as theological . Its reality and definition are determined by Scripture, but the word itself is not found in Scripture. As we have said in earlier studies, the word âTrinityâ is another word like thisâ¦ ANOTHER CLARIFICATION I WOULD LIKE TO MAKE HERE AT THE BEGINNING is that excellent scholars, men I have come to trust and admire, disagree on their definitions of âPredestinationââ¦ SOME SCHOLARS PREFER TO DEFINE âPREDESTINATIONâ IN THE BROADEST possible sense, holding that the word applies to every expression of the will of God regarding all human beings â believers and unbelievers alike, angels, and all events. Respectfully, for various reasons I trust will become evident in the course of this study, I have a problem accepting these definitions with confidenceâ¦ FOR EXAMPLE, APPLYING âPREDESTINATIONâ TO ANGELS, as a number of theologians doâ¦ From one theology book this statement: âThe (evil angels) who kept not their first estate are destined to the lake of fire.â â Chaferâ¦ THIS THINKING COMES FROM MATTHEW 25:41â¦ NAS Matthew 25:41 âThen He will also say to those on His left, âDepart from Me, accursed ones, into the eternal fire which has been prepared for the devil and his angels; I DO NOT ARGUE THAT GOD HAS âPREPAREDâ THE LAKE OF FIRE FOR SATAN and his angels. Matthew 25:41 and Revelation 20:10 clearly tell us that. But I have trouble saying this is predestination. For one thing, the word âpredestinedâ is not in this verse. The word here in Matthew 25:41 is âpreparedâ ( á¼ÏÎ¿Î¹Î¼á½±Î¶Ï [ heh-toi-mahd-zo ]), not âpredestined. The meaning in Matthew 25:41 is that God had previously prepared a place. I believe you will see that clearly is not the meaning of âPredestination.â There is more I could say, but I will move on. I am unconvinced that Godâs dealings with Satan and the evil angels who followed him in rebellion is technically âPredestinationââ¦ I AM OFFERING A DEFINITON OF âPREDESTINATIONâ FROM a Greek teacher, an exegete, not a theologianâ¦ My definition is admittedly smaller, narrower, and not likely to be found in theological textbooks, but I would defend it as sound. It is based upon the uses of the Greek verb âpredestinate,â particularly how Paul uses the word, and especially how Paul uses the word in Ephesians 1:5â¦ IT IS VERY DIFFICULT TO COME UP WITH A CONCISE AND comprehensive definition of âPredestinationââ¦ MY SEMINARY DEFINITION OF âPREDESTINATION,â which this week I looked up in one of my seminary notebooks reads, Predestination is that part of the Decree whereby God sets limits around that which He purposes for the elect so that each elect person will be placed as an adult son . It is my prayer that after this study and next weekâs study on âAdoption,â you will come to understand that definition and come to fully appreciate the loving doctrine of âPredestinationââ¦ YOU WILL REMEMBER THERE IS ALSO A DIFFERENCE AMONG SCHOLARS AS to whether the phrase âin loveâ goes with v. 4 or with v. 5. I shared with you previously that in my studied opinion, I believe âin loveâ goes with v. 4: âthat we should be holy and blameless before Him in love.â This interpretation is reflected in the KJV, the NKJ, the NET, and the NLT translations. The NAS, which I have been using in our study, along with the ESV and NIV translations connect the phrase âin loveâ to v. 5: âin love He predestined us to adoption as sonsââ¦ AS I HAVE MENTIONED BEFORE, VV. 3-14 OF THE FIRST CHAPTER of Ephesians comprise one extended sentence in the Greek text; it is the longest sentence in the entire Bible. Because this lengthy sentence is not punctuated in the original language, it is often difficult for scholars and Bible translators to decide where one clause ends and another begins. Such is the case with vv. 4 and 5â¦ I HAVE STUDIED THIS QUESTION FOR YEARS, AND WHILE WE simply cannot know for certain whether âin loveâ belongs with v. 4 or with v. 5, I am treating the phrase as part of v. 4, so we are beginning v. 5â¦ NAS Ephesians 1:5 He predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the kind intention of His will, (For Greek students, my reasoning is this: âpredestinedâ is an aorist participle; it is not the main verb. The main verb in vv. 4-5 is âchoseâ [aorist middle indicative]. So âpredestinedâ is modifying âchose.â Therefore, if âin loveâ [one word in Greek] is meant to refer to Godâs action in predestining [as NAS, ESV, and NIV indicate], which is describing more fully how God chose, it would seem more likely that Paul would have placed the phrase âin loveâ with the main verb, not the secondary participle: âjust as He chose us in love in Himâ or âjust as He chose us in Him in love.â Admittedly, we cannot be certain either way.)â¦ âON THE WHOLE IT IS PREFERABLETO ATTACH âIN LOVEâ TO WHAT PRECEDES so that it is viewed as part of the goal election is intended to achieve, namely, a life before God which is holy and blameless and lived in love.â â OâBrienâ¦ GOD CHOSE US, AND GOD PREDESTINED USâ¦ PAUL IS USING THESE TWO COMPLEX WORDS TO EXPLAIN GODâS ACTIONS âbefore the foundation of the worldâ on our behalf. âChosenâ and âpredestinedâ may indeed be difficult words, but they are wonderful words for the believer. When properly studied, âchosenâ and âpredestinedâ speak of Godâs love and purpose for us, and assure us of our everlasting life with Him in heavenâ¦ PAUL SAYS THAT THE PURPOSE OF PREDESTINATION IS ADOPTIONâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:5 He predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the kind intention of His will, âBECAUSE OF GODâS PREDESTINATION, BELIEVERS ARE ADOPTED sons and daughters in His family. Nothing could be finer than to belong to God!â â Garnerâ¦ NEXT WEEK WE WILL LEARN ABOUT THE FASCINATING SUBJECT OF âAdoptionââ¦ WHILE I AM QUICK TO ACKNOWLEDGE THE DIFFICULTIES in accurately defining the word âPredestination,â as a Greek teacher who has studied this word for more than a few years it is my humble opinion that it is not as difficult as is commonly thought. I think if we start with an understanding of what the word itself means â and this, remember, must come from the verb form, since the noun form is not found in Scripture, and then maintain that understanding as we attempt to determine its meaning in Scripture and its theological meaning to us as believers, although we may not be able to speak about âPredestinationâ dogmatically with complete assurance, we are nevertheless unlikely to be too far offâ¦ âPREDESTINATIONâ COMES FROM THE GREEK VERB ÏÏÎ¿Î¿Ïá½·Î¶Ï ( pra-ah-reed-zo )â¦ BDAG, the leading Greek lexicon in the world today, defines ÏÏÎ¿Î¿Ïá½·Î¶Ï ( pra-ah-reed-zo ) as to decide beforehand, predetermine â¦ A ONE WORD DEFINITION OF âPREDESTINATIONâ IS âPREDETERMINATIONââ¦ When God predestines us He predetermines

content: About Systematic Theology â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego This âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video, presented by Pastor Paul of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego , addresses the topic of systematic theology. Systematic theology may not be a very familiar phrase, but it is an important one. Barabbas Road Church in San Diego even offers a class about it. Systematic theology is the orderly study of God and all of His creation and doings. There are about ten sections within systematic theology, and each section is connected to the other. Each section covers a different doctrine within Christian theology. The first section is called theology proper and focuses on God the Father and the reasons for His existence. The second is bibliology, which is the study of the scripture as the inerrant and infallible Word of God. The third section is anthropology, which is the doctrine of man. Next is hamartiology, or the doctrine of sin. Then comes soteriology, which is the doctrine of salvation, pneumatology, or the doctrine of the Holy Spirit, ecclesiology, which is the doctrine of the church, and eschatology, or the doctrine of the future and the end times. Last comes Christology, the doctrine of Christ. When each of these individual doctrines is studied, each and every Bible verse that pertains to that specific doctrine is compiled so that every facet and aspect of the doctrine can be studied. It helps theologians understand exactly what the Bible teaches about a specific topic. Systematic theology, however, considers how all of these doctrines work together to make up the teachings of the Christian faith. As each aspect works together and compliments each other, it helps us understand the world as a whole in a comprehensive view. If one doctrine does not follow what the Bible says, then the others cannot connect to it. For example, if it were true that man is mostly good, then he would not have need for a Savior and there would be no reason for Jesus. However, man is sinful and needs a Savior, which paves the way for Jesus. Each doctrine compliments the others. God works in each doctrine to create a âwebâ of theology. Even though each doctrine can be studied solely, together they form a tight system of strong theology. Christians need strong theology. Studying it systematically can shed greater light on how the teachings of the Bible are all connected. You can watch the whole Whiteboad Wednesday video below.

content: The Decree â Part II THIS IS YET ANOTHER BLOG DEALING WITH THE DEEPEST THING OF GOD from the opening chapter of the great book of Ephesiansâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3-4 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, 4 just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him. PAULâS INTRODUCTION TO EPHESIANS VV. 3-14, WHICH IS HIS OFFICIAL introduction to his great epistle (vv. 1-2 is a greeting), is an example of Godâs determinative will. Godâs determinative will is synonymous to His Decree. Though the Greek word for âDecree,â Î²Î¿ÏÎ»á½´Î½ ( boo-lay ), is only found in v. 11, the concept is clearly present throughout. Paul is talking about the things God determined before the foundation of the world, things that have happened or will happen without question. Listen to v. 11 againâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:11 also we have obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to His purpose who works all things after the counsel of His will , HIS DETERMINATIVE WILL. HIS DETERMINATIVE IS THE DECREEâ¦ GODâS DETERMINATIVE WILL IS, AS YOU MIGHT EXPECT TO HEAR, absolutely free, unencumbered by circumstance. âBeing alone when His decree was made, His determinations were influenced by no other being. Aside from the fact that He must act according to His wisdom and holiness, He was free to do or not to do. Within the sphere of His perfections, He could do what He would.â â Chaferâ¦ NAS Isaiah 40:13-14 Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, Or as His counselor has informed Him? 14 With whom did He consult and who gave Him understanding? And who taught Him in the path of justice and taught Him knowledge, And informed Him of the way of understanding? THE DECREE OF GOD WAS THE EXPRESSION OF THE FREE WILL OF GOD, the sovereign will of Godâ¦ A BRIEF BUT IMPORTANT OBSERVATION ABOUT FREE WILL: Though some Christians chaff at any mention that diminishes in any way the free will of man, I must nevertheless humbly say that the freedom of will we humans possess cannot be compared to the free will of God. Only Godâs will is entirely free. Our freedom is conditioned by our humanity, the fact we are limited created beingsâ¦ THERE IS GODâS ABSOLUTE SOVEREIGNTY, AND THERE IS ALSO MANâS FREE willâ¦ How they both can exist together at the same time is an enigma, but the Scripture insists both are trueâ¦ AS I HAVE MENTIONED MORE THAN ONCE IN PREVIOUS BLOGS, the best word I have found in my studies over the years to describe this enigma is âantimonyâ Antinomy says that two seemingly contradictory truths â incredible as it may at first sound â can and sometimes do exists simultaneously. Light is an example; it is both wavelength and particle. Science says this cannot be, yet scientists are forced to deal with the dualistic reality of light all the same. And then there is Jesus; is He not 100% God and 100% man at the same time? That canât be, our human minds tell us, and yet we know it is true. Antinomyâ¦ SOMEHOW, SOMEWAY, AT LEAST IN SOME AREAS, IT IS A âBOTH/ANDâ SITUATIONâ¦ The reality is that God is absolutely sovereign. He knows all things and He ordains all things. We must say that He does indeed ordain all things or we cannot say that He has a perfect plan for His creation. He could not be said to have a perfect plan if there are things He does not know or allows to exist apart from His control. God is entirely sovereign. And yet, somehow, someway, at the same time God is sovereign, man possesses a free will. Antinomyâ¦ âGOD AS CREATOR HAS THE RIGHT TO RULE HIS UNIVERSE IN ANY WAY He sees fit consistent with His own attributes. If He should choose to delegate spheres of autonomy (human freedom to make decisions â TAR) to His creatures, this in no way limits His sovereignty. By His omniscient foreknowledge of both eventualities and non-eventual possibilities, God orchestrates and arranges those events He chooses without coercing the wills of the human moral agents involved.â â Olsonâ¦ I TRIED TO COME UP WITH AN ANALOGY THAT MIGHT HELP YOU formulate in your minds this difficult concept regarding Godâs sovereignty and simultaneously manâs free will, and I came up with this. Imagine an ancient king who rules an imaginary kingdom. The king is sovereign; his rule is unchallenged. He makes all the laws and renders all the punishment. At the same time the king is exercising his sovereign rule, the individual subjects of his kingdom enjoy free will. They make decisions about what crops to plant, how many children to have, and what to eat for the day. Make sense? A sovereign king need not restrict the free choices of his peopleâ¦ IâLL SAY MORE ABOUT OUR FREE WILL next week when we talk about predestination (Ephesians 1:5, 11)â¦ NOW, LET ME QUICKLY GIVE YOU AN EXAMPLE OF GODâS DESIROUS WILLâ¦ NAS 1 Timothy 2:3-4 This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, 4 who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. GOD âDESIRESâ ALL TO BE SAVED; HE DOES NOT DETERMINE THAT ALL WILL be savedâ¦ That, of course, would deny manâs âfreeâ will and make grace and love and faith and obedience all but meaninglessâ¦ (The Greek word in 1 Tim 2:4 is not boulh , [ bou-lay ] but qe,lw [ thay-lo ], a word that may be seen to be of a lesser degree than boulh , [ bou-lay ]; qe,lw [ thay-lo ] can be translated âwishâ or âdesireâ â God wishes or desires that all be saved; He does not determine that all be saved.)â¦ âTHE DECREEâ IS THE TERM THEOLOGIANS APPLY TO THE FACT THAT BEFORE the foundations of the world the three Persons of the Godhead sovereignly planned the creation of the universe and all the events that would happen in it, including the salvation of certain peopleâ¦ âWITH GOD THERE IS ONE IMMUTABLE DECREE EMBRACING IN ITSELF every detail (of the creation, the maintenance, and eventually the renewing of the world â TAR), even the falling of a sparrow.â â Chaferâ¦ NET Matthew 10:29 Arenât two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Fatherâs will. AND FROM ACTS 15:18â¦ KJV Acts 15:18 Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world. âTHE TERM âDIVINE DECREEâ IS AN ATTEMPT TO GATHER UP INTO ONE designation that to which the Scriptures refer by various designations, the divine purpose (Eph 1:11), determinate counsel (Acts 2:23), foreknowledge (1 Peter 1:2), election (Eph 1:3 and 1 Thess 1:4), predestination (Eph 1:5, 11; Rom 8:30), the divine will (Eph 1:11), and the divine good pleasure (Eph 1:9).â â Chaferâ¦ âTHE DOCTRINE OF DIVINE DECREE IS ONLY ANOTHER METHOD OF assigning to God the position of first cause of all that exists. There is one comprehensive plan in which all things have their place and by which they proceed.â â Chaferâ¦ AFTER STUDYING THIS CHALLENGING SUBJECT ALL WEEK, MY HUMBLE definition of âThe Decreeâ is this: The Decree is Godâs sovereign purposeful plan for the creation of the universe and everything that happens thereafter â¦ CAN WE NOT ALL SEE AND APPRECIATE WHAT GODâS DECREE MEANS TO US?â¦ For one thing it means that God is in complete control of everything that is happening in the world and happening to us. There is immense comfort in knowing that God has a plan. And He has a purpose. There is divine purpose in our sufferings. God does not choose to reveal to us all the details of His plan, but Scripture assures us He does indeed have a plan. There is great comfort in knowing this fact, brothers and sisters!â¦ âTHERE IS A WORTHY REASON FOR ALL THAT GOD HAS EVER DONE or will do. Even His permission of evil will, like the wrath of man, can be seen to praise Him.â â Chaferâ¦ NIV Psalm 76:10 Surely your wrath against men brings you praise, NAS Romans 11:33 Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! content: The Decree Part I FOR MY FIRST WORDS I WOULD LIKE TO SAY THAT OUR SUBJECT FOR this morning towers over us like the peak of an enormous mountain. This is a heavy one. After reading all Iâve written, I believe youâll see why I went to two parts. Even in two blogs I can but hope to touch the hem of Godâs garment in my understating of âThe Decree.â There is much I confess I do not know about âThe Decreeâ of God. There is much, I suggest, human beings cannot know. Much of this subject is just Godâs business. I cannot help but think of Isaiah 55:8-9, as I often do when I realize I am dealing with thoughts higher than I. But touching the hem of Godâs garment is intellectually achievable and it is, I think youâll agree, is a glorious thing and we can be thankful forâ¦ NAS Isaiah 55:8-9 âFor My thoughts are not your thoughts, Neither are your ways My ways,â declares the LORD. 9 âFor as the heavens are higher than the earth, So are My ways higher than your ways, And My thoughts than your thoughts. LORD, HELP US TO COMPREHEND WHAT WE CAN COMPREHEND of this grand doctrine of Your Wordâ¦ THIS BLOG IS IN MANY WAYS A CONTINUATION OF A PREVIOUS BLOG: âChosen by God,â as well as a prelude to a coming blog on âPredestination.â All of these deep subjects are expressions of Godâs sovereignty, His sovereign will, and His sovereign ways of dealing with His creation â in other words, His businessâ¦ âSOVEREIGN,â YOU WILL REMEMBER, IS THE WORD WE USE TO REFER TO THE fact that God is in complete and uninterrupted control of His creation. Sovereign means that God is the supreme and unchallengeable Ruler of all things â including every human being and every situation â and that He has absolute authority over all things. Authority means that He has the right to His universal rule. He can do as He wishes and answer to no oneâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3-4 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, 4 just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him. In love HERE AT THE BEGINNING, LET ME POINT OUT A BEAUTIFUL TRUTH concerning the Lord Jesus Christ. We believe Jesus is Lord, that is He is God. In order to be God, One has to be eternal. He had to have existed before creation. Look at your Bibles again: it says that God chose us âin Him,â that is, in Christ, âbefore the foundations of the world.â if you think that through for a moment you will see that Jesus then existed along with God the Father in eternity before creation. That means He is eternal. That means He is Godâ¦ THE PHRASE âBEFORE THE FOUNDATION OF THE WORLDâ LEADS US INTO this weekâs study of âThe Decree.â I could have called this blog âBefore the Foundation of the Worldââ¦ ââBEFORE THE FOUNDATION OF THE WORLDâ DENOTES THE TIME of the election.â â Hoehnerâ¦ THAT IS A QUOTE; WE MIGHT QUESTION THE USE OF THE WORD âTIME,â since there was no âtimeâ as we know it before the foundation of the world. Time as we know it did not exist until God created the world of space and time. And yet, I donât want to be critical. I know well that in talking of the things of God we must often resort to a kind of language of accommodation in order to communicate all but inexpressible thingsâ¦ LET ME GIVE YOU A COUPLE OF STATEMENTS TO KEEP IN YOUR THOUGHTS as I attempt to communicate the great doctrine of the âThe Decree.â One statement is that time exists as a part of eternity. In the sense of time as we know it, eternity is timeless. The other statement, which is another way at coming at this difficult topic, is that eternity is outside time. Scholars use both perspectives to discuss their relationship. I prefer the former, that time exists within the limitless horizons of eternityâ¦ YET ANOTHER WAY OF CONSIDERING THE SUBJECT OF ETERNITY IS the approach our English dictionaries take. They say that eternity is a seemingly endless or immeasurable amount of timeâ¦ MY AMERICAN HERITAGE COLLEGE DICTIONARY SAYS THAT TIME IS a nonspatial continuum in which events occur in apparently irreversible succession from the past through the present to the future, a duration. That is, of course, only one connotation of the word time. My dictionary had 14 connotations in all. Bottom line: itâs difficult for us human beings to put our minds around the concept of time, let alone eternityâ¦ NAS Isaiah 55:8-9 âFor My thoughts are not your thoughts, Neither are your ways My ways,â declares the LORD. 9 âFor as the heavens are higher than the earth, So are My ways higher than your ways, And My thoughts than your thoughts. BUT THE BIBLE TELLS US IN EPHESIANS 1:4 THAT IN ETERNITY BEFORE TIME was, God made some decisions and formulated a plan. Those decisions and plan constitute what theologians refer to as âThe Decree.â One of those decisions by God was that He would choose some people to form His body of believers on earth. He did this âbefore the foundation of the worldââ¦ THE WORD âFOUNDATIONâ IS AN INTERESTING WORD IN ITS GREEK ORIGINâ¦ The Greek word is ÎºÎ±ÏÎ±Î²Î¿Î»Î· , ( k a-ta-ba-lay ). It is a compound word consisting of ÎºÎ±ÏÎ± ( k a-ta) , which basically means down , and Î²Î¿Î»Î· , ( ba-lay ), meaning throw . A foundation is literally something that is thrown down (1. the act of laying someth.. down, with implication of providing a base for someth., foundation. â BDAG). Readily connected with the idea of founding is the sense beginning â¦ NAS John 1:1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. THE VERBS IN THIS UNFORGETTABLE VERSE ARE ALL IN THE IMPERFECT tense. The imperfect tense denotes continuous action in the past. This fact strongly implies â if not proves â that before the beginning, God already was. God does not have a beginning; He created the beginningâ¦ AND BEFORE THE BEGINNING, PAUL SAYS, WE WERE âCHOSEN BY GOD.â Our human, three-dimensional minds can only go so far on that thought. The beginning is hard enough to comprehend; before the beginning is all Godâs businessâ¦ AND YET, HE IS GRACIOUS ENOUGH TO TELL US SOMETHING ABOUT IT in verses like Ephesians 1:4. For example, we can know that before the beginning there was God, and that He was already doing something for usâ¦ WHEN YOU PONDER EPHESIANS 1:3-4 â I MEAN WHEN YOU REALLY THINK it through, you see that these two verses clearly tell us who God is and who we are. It is not an exaggeration to say that these two verses â when properly studied through and thought out â comprise the entire Christian lifeâ¦ NOW LET US CONSIDER THE WORD âDECREE.â What exactly are we talking about when we use the word?â¦ A âDECREEâ IS DEFINED IN OUR ENGLISH DICTIONARIES AS an authoritative order having the force of law; it is the judgment of a courtâ¦ The verb form of decree means to ordain, establish, or decide by decreeâ¦ THE WORD ITSELF IS FOUND OFTEN IN THE BIBLE. It is used 41 times (BibleWorks search on the noun), 40 times in the O.T.â¦ The N.T. occurrence is one which you are familiarâ¦ KJV Luke 2:1 And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed. THAT, OF COURSE, IS THE DECREE THAT PLAYED A PART IN THE BIRTH of the Lord Jesusâ¦ THE GREEK USED IN LUKE 2:1 IS Î´Î¿Î³Î¼Î± ( dog-ma )â¦ 1. a formal statement concerning rules or regulations that are to be observed â BDAG. Another lexicon (Friberg) defines the Greek word as an opinion , a (public) decree . This Greek word is obviously where we get our English word âdogma.â A dogma is a code of belief, a creed, a system of tenets. You can see that the meaning of our English word for âdecreeâ is very close to the meaning of the word in the Greekâ¦ IN THE O.T., THE FIRST USE OF THE WORD âDECREEâ IS FOUND INâ¦ NAS 2 Chronicles 30:5 So they established a decree to circulate a proclamation throughout all Israel from Beersheba even to Dan, that they should come to celebrate the Passover to the LORD God of Israel at Jerusalem. content: Chosen By God Part II âCHOSEN BY GOD,â AN ABBREVIATED INVESTIGATION OF THE DEEP DOCTRINE of election in two parts from Ephesians 1:4â¦ âChosen by Godâ and âelectionâ are synonymous terms; they both refer to the same biblical doctrineâ¦ NAS Ephesians 1:3-4 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him. In love.. LAST WEEK, I ENDED PART I BY EMPHASIZING THE WORD âSOVEREGNTYââ¦ It is all but impossible to fully grasp the meaning of being chosen by God without understanding Godâs sovereignty. ANOTHER WORD ALONG THESE ESSENTIAL LINES of defining and comprehending the interrelated terms of election is relationship â¦ Inherent in the deep doctrines of election, predestination, adoption, and foreknowledge is relationship. One of the wonders of the world is that Almighty God desires to be in relationship with sinful human beings. Oh, to be sure, He cannot be in relationship with sinful human beings â His holiness will not permit it â until they have been transformed by salvation, but His desire is real and continuous. In all these deep doctrines of salvation, one thing that can be said of all of them is that they speak of relationship. In all of these deep doctrines, God is seeking relationship with manâ¦ IN SPITE OF THE DIFFICULTIES, THERE IS A GREAT BLESSING that awaits the believer willing humbly to be taught by this great doctrine that teaches such deep truth about God and His workings with mankindâ¦ IT IS NOT AN IRRESPONSIBLE EXAGGERATION TO SAY THAT in the 12 verses of the introduction to the book of Ephesians (vv. 3-14) one finds the deepest truths about God to be found in all of Scriptureâ¦ If we can get a grasp of these deep truths, our lives cannot help but be immensely enrichedâ¦ THE MORE WE KNOW ABOUT GOD, THE MORE WE CAN APPRECIATE HIM â to know Him is to love Him. The more we love God, the more we will want to serve Him. The more we serve Him in obedience to His Word, the richer our lives will be, for our very purpose here on earth is to love, serve, and glorify God. True satisfaction lies not in serving the self as the world insists, but in serving God as the Bible commandsâ¦ THE BIBLE INARGUABLY STATES THAT GOD CHOSE BELIEVERS to be saved. Regardless of how difficult or even unfair it may seem to some Christians, this is the Word of God and must be accepted and believedâ¦ GOD THE FATHER HAS ELECTED A NUMBER OF PEOPLE TO be given to God the Son for the purpose of building His church. If you are a Christian you must believe this because it is the clear teaching of Scriptureâ¦ âTO CONTEND AS SOME HAVE THAT GOD, TO BE FAIR AND IMPARTIAL, must bestow His greatest riches of blessing upon all alike is, as we have said, to sit in judgment upon the Creator, to deny Godâs sovereign right to order his creation as He will, and to deprive God of His freedom to bring about His perfect plan as He wills.â â Chafer/TARâ¦ BEFORE ANY CONDEMN GOD FOR BEING UNFAIR, ONE MUST FIRST acknowledge the fact that all human beings are spiritually bankruptâ¦ NKJ Romans 3:11 There is none who understands; There is none who seeks after God. THE PERSON WHO ARGUES THAT GOD IS UNFAIR FAILS TO REALIZE THAT God is under no obligation to save anyone. As many scholars have rightly saidâ¦ THE QUESTION IS NOT âWHY DOES GOD NOT JUST SAVE EVERYONE?â but âwhy does He save anyone?ââ¦ NAS Romans 3:23 for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, IF GOD HAD NOT TAKEN THE INITIATIVE TO SAVE SOME, no one would have been ever believedâ¦ IN THIS MESSAGE THIS MORNING THERE IS VALUABLE TRUTH that can enlighten us as to the mind of God, teach us lessons that will prevent us from wrong thinking about God and His dealings with us, humble us as to the sovereignty of God, and comfort us in the midst of our struggles in this lifeâ¦ GOD DID NOT CHOOSE EVERYONE BECAUSE IT WAS NOT HIS PLAN to do so. He has a perfect plan and He is not obligated to consult anyone or to explain Himself. He is sovereign. He is Godâ¦ I WILL DISCUSS THESE DEEP THINGS FURTHER IN A COMING BLOG on âPredestinationââ¦ ONE OF THE ENGLISH DEFINITIONS OF âCHOICEâ IS âthe power, right, or liberty to chooseââ¦ Only God has the power , the right , and the perfect freedom to chooseâ¦ NAS Daniel 4:35 â¦But He does according to His will in the host of heaven And among the inhabitants of earth; And no one can ward off His hand Or say to Him, âWhat hast Thou done?â YOU PROBABLY DONâT NEED ME TO TELL YOU THAT GOD IS SOVEREIGN. Although we use the word in common language, especially to describe kings and presidents, courts and countries, but in one immediate sense, there is only one to whom the word should be applied. Only God possesses absolute authority and has complete independenceâ¦ SOVEREIGNTY MEANS THAT GOD IS THE BOSS AND THAT WE ARE notâ¦ BECAUSE OF THAT FACT, THIS MESSAGE MAY CONFRONT MANY READERSâ sensibilities. This message may present a side of God you may have avoided understanding â or maybe you have understood it all too well and have chosen to live as if it were not a factâ¦ an undeniable fact, a changeless, eternal factâ¦ SOME, INCLUDING MANY SOUTHERN BAPTISTS, BELIEVE THAT election should be explained as God in eternity looking down the corridors of time, seeing that we would choose Him, and then choosing usâ¦ With all due respect, that is wrong. That view is wrong for more than one reason. Not only does such a theology go against Scripture (cf. John 15:16; Rom 3:11), but in such a view man then becomes sovereign. Man first makes the choice; God is only responding to manâs choice. This is not the biblical view of election. This view elevates man, makes him responsible for his own salvationâ¦ BUT MAN DOES NOT CHOOSE GOD FIRST; GOD CHOOSES MAN FIRSTâ¦ NAS John 15:16 âYou did not choose Me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remainâ¦ IS THAT NOT CLEAR? If you believe the Bible is Godâs Word, you cannot ignore this central point. It is God who does the initial choosingâ¦ GOD CHOSE US BEFORE WE WERE BORN. The Bible says God chose believers before the foundation of world! Listen to these beautiful words from Ephesians 1â¦ NKJ Ephesians 1:3-4 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before Him in love, THAT IS PROBABLY THE DEFINITIVE WORD IN SCRIPTURE ON ELECTION. That is the essence of existence. That is the wisdom of the world in summary. These words in Ephesians 1:3-4 are some of the most wonderful, most challenging words in the entire Bible. They tell us of our reality in Christ, and they tell us of the privilege and responsibility we have as believersâ¦ BUT SOMEONE SAYS, DIDNâT I ALSO CHOOSE GOD? What about manâs free will? I must be brief, but will take these questions up again in the following weeks, Lord willing. For now, let me give you a studied answer in a quickly drawn imageâ¦ IMAGINE TWO SIDES OF A MOUNTAIN AS YOU ARE STARING AT IT from a distance. You see the two opposite sides of the mountain ascending at convergent angels toward the top. Imagine one side being Godâs sovereignty and the other side manâs free will. You look up to see the point where you imagine and anticipate the two sides meeting, but that point is lost in the clouds. Can you say that the two sides do not meet simply because you cannot see them meeting? God does not tell us how they meet. Manâs free will and Godâs sovereign may seem like they cannot meet, but somehow they do. title: Decision Making and the Will of God
excerpt: Decision Making and the Will of God â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube presentation, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego tackles the subject of making personalâ¦
content: Decision Making and the Will of God â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube presentation, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego tackles the subject of making personal decisions while adhering to the will of God. Is it possible to have the freedom of choice while obeying the moral will of God? This topic focuses on three areas: decision making, Godâs sovereignty, and our freedom. The only way to achieve true freedom to decide is to let Godâs sovereign will preside over your life. Augustine said it this way: âlove God and do what you want.â This expression does not mean we have the freedom to break the law or to do evil to others while claiming to love God; rather, it means that if we truly love God, we have the desire to do good things. Romans 8:28 says that all things will work out for those who love God. A question that poses a dilemmais this: does God have two wills or three wills? God has a perceptive will and a sovereign will. His perceptive will gives us guidelines and boundaries to live by, like the Ten Commandments. His sovereign will, or holy will, can contradict his perceptive will. For example, Godâs sovereign will was that Jesus, His only son, would have to die on the cross for the sins of the world to accomplish Godâs holy purpose. Yet is there another will that God has, one that He intends for each individual? How does a person know the exact will of God for his or her life and make sure to get it right? Some people fear that they will decide the wrong thing and that they will stray from the will of God. A person might wonder things like, should I get married to this person now, or someone else later? Should I attend this college in Chicago? Should I try going to this church in San Diego? We do not need to fear our options, but rather we needto seek Godâs guidance. God wants us to seek Him and come to Him in prayer. He has given us the freedom to make our own choices within His sovereign guidance. When we do our best to follow Godâs moral will, we have the freedom to make our own decisions. Even when we sin, God can take a bad situation and turn it around for His glory and His purposes, like he did for Joseph in the Old Testament. Trust in Godâs holy will, read His Word for guidance in life, and be free to make decisions. You can watch the whole Whiteboad Wednesday video below.

title: Preaching that Punctures
excerpt: Preaching that Punctures â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video segment, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses different styles of preaching. He notes thatâ¦
content: Preaching that Punctures â Barabbas Road Church in San Diego In this âWhiteboard Wednesdayâ YouTube video segment, Pastor Matt of Barabbas Road Church in San Diego discusses different styles of preaching. He notes that his church in San Diego has a certain âflavorâ that is different from other churches in the area, for example, and that these differences occur due to differences in preaching methodology. The two terms used to describe this difference in methodology, or epistemology (the study of what distinguishes belief from opinion), are synthesis and antitheses. The methodology of antithesis uses logic to shed light on the truth. This type of logic says that a specific thing cannot equal a non-form of that specific thing. Therefore, what the Bible says is truth. If the Bible is true, then Jesus is truth. This conclusion is drawn using logic. Synthesis, on the other hand, finds truth in similarities. This methodology begins with similarities and builds truth from common ground shared between two or more entities. It seeks to find a common denominator between religions and groups. An example of synthesis thinking is the âcoexistâ bumper sticker, which exudes the message that all religions can exist together peacefully. Churches that practice a synthesis style of preaching might adopt vague âwhat we believeâ statements in an effort to welcome as many people with different views and backgrounds as possible. However, the synthesis methodology contradicts the Bible. Theologian Francis Schaeffer said that âthe church has adopted and lost antithesis.â He suggested that three things must be done to bring the church at large back to a methodology of antithesis. First, historic doctrine â Biblical truths that have developed over time â must be upheld. Second, the church must maintain logical and consistent answers. If a curious person asks a logical question, use scripture to help that person find a logical answer. And third, the Christian church as a whole must exhibit God as the ultimate authority in life. Truth is seen in Christ alone. If the Christian church adheres to a logical methodology and the Bible is true, then all other religions are not true. Godâs Word is truth. Live out your life according to what the Bible says. The Church must come together and communicate the truth, and preaching should be sharp and pointed.
